submissions.name: Academic Citing License

curated_rwp.rejection_reason: Never approved. The license required citation in academic papers, which goes beyond what copyright licenses can enforce.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Proposes the Academic Citing License (MIT with a citation condition), requiring scientific publications using the program to cite a specified reference, and asks whether it conforms to the OSD.
timeline.point_zh: 提出 Academic Citing License（MIT 加引用条件），要求使用该程序的科学出版物须引用指定文献，并询问是否符合 OSD。
timeline.point: Proposes the Academic Citing License (MIT with a citation condition), requiring scientific publications using the program to cite a specified reference, and asks whether it conforms to the OSD.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Points out that the citation condition is a restriction on use of program output, does not conform to the OSD, and suggests using an already-approved license with a citation reminder instead.
timeline.point_zh: 指出引用条件是对程序输出的使用限制，不符合 OSD，建议改用已批准许可证并辅以引用提醒。
timeline.point: Points out that the citation condition is a restriction on use of program output, does not conform to the OSD, and suggests using an already-approved license with a citation reminder instead.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Through a series of pointed questions, demonstrates that the condition restricts use of program output and recommends requesting rather than requiring citation.
timeline.point_zh: 通过一系列追问指出该条件是对程序输出使用的限制，建议改为请求而非强制引用。
timeline.point: Through a series of pointed questions, demonstrates that the condition restricts use of program output and recommends requesting rather than requiring citation.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Explains that SourceForge requires software to conform to the OSD and needs OSI approval before it will accept a new license for hosting.
timeline.point_zh: 说明 SourceForge 要求软件符合 OSD，需先获 OSI 批准方可托管。
timeline.point: Explains that SourceForge requires software to conform to the OSD and needs OSI approval before it will accept a new license for hosting.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Argues that the citation condition does not restrict fields of endeavor and does not violate the wording or intent of OSD #6.
timeline.point_zh: 辩称引用条件不涉及使用领域限制，认为不违反 OSD #6 的措辞与意图。
timeline.point: Argues that the citation condition does not restrict fields of endeavor and does not violate the wording or intent of OSD #6.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Clarifies that the citation condition applies only to journals used for communication among scientists, and discusses output copyright ownership and traceability.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清引用条件仅针对科学家间交流的期刊，并讨论输出版权归属与可追溯性。
timeline.point: Clarifies that the citation condition applies only to journals used for communication among scientists, and discusses output copyright ownership and traceability.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Thanks David and indicates acceptance of his advice.
timeline.point_zh: 向 David 致谢，表示接受其建议。
timeline.point: Thanks David and indicates acceptance of his advice.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Explains that copyright holders have no right to restrict day-to-day use, considers the citation restriction unenforceable, and advises against including it in the license.
timeline.point_zh: 解释版权持有人无权限制日常使用，认为引用限制不可执行，不建议加入许可证。
timeline.point: Explains that copyright holders have no right to restrict day-to-day use, considers the citation restriction unenforceable, and advises against including it in the license.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Uses Trove database data to show that SourceForge actually hosts a large number of non-OSI-approved and public-domain projects, challenging its stated policy.
timeline.point_zh: 通过 Trove 数据指出 SourceForge 实际托管了大量非 OSI 批准/公共领域项目，质疑其声称的政策。
timeline.point: Uses Trove database data to show that SourceForge actually hosts a large number of non-OSI-approved and public-domain projects, challenging its stated policy.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Corrects the statistics: public-domain projects need not have OSI-approved licenses yet remain open source, and most of the 948 are miscategorized.
timeline.point_zh: 纠正统计：公共领域项目无需 OSI 许可证但仍属开源，且 948 个多为分类错误。
timeline.point: Corrects the statistics: public-domain projects need not have OSI-approved licenses yet remain open source, and most of the 948 are miscategorized.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Considers mandatory citation an indirect demand for recognition, questioning why the normal peer-review process cannot be relied upon.
timeline.point_zh: 认为强制引用相当于间接索取认可，质疑为何不依赖正常的同行评审流程。
timeline.point: Considers mandatory citation an indirect demand for recognition, questioning why the normal peer-review process cannot be relied upon.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Notes that most public-domain projects he audited had upstream copyright issues, and SourceForge refused to conduct a review.
timeline.point_zh: 指出其审核的公共领域项目多存在上游版权问题，SourceForge 拒绝进行审核。

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License

timeline.snippet: Stands firm, reiterating that most public-domain projects he audited had serious licensing problems, and emphasizing that public domain is not a license.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Clarifies that CC NonCommercial licenses restrict distribution and public performance rather than everyday use, and therefore do not constitute restrictions on use.

timeline.point: Clarifies that CC NonCommercial licenses restrict distribution and public performance rather than everyday use, and therefore do not constitute restrictions on use.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Though not a fan of the proposal, asks whether it actually conforms to the OSD.

timeline.point: Though not a fan of the proposal, asks whether it actually conforms to the OSD.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Expresses sympathy for the submitter, noting he has personally encountered inadequate attribution in computer science.
timeline.point_zh: 表示理解提交者，自己也在计算机科学领域亲历过引用缺失的情况。
timeline.point: Expresses sympathy for the submitter, noting he has personally encountered inadequate attribution in computer science.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: As a composer, challenges the claim that performance is not use.
timeline.point_zh: 以作曲者身份质疑"表演不是使用"的说法。
timeline.point: As a composer, challenges the claim that performance is not use.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Explains that in copyright law, performance refers to public performance, and private use does not constitute a performance.
timeline.point_zh: 解释版权法中表演指公开表演，私人使用不构成表演。
timeline.point: Explains that in copyright law, performance refers to public performance, and private use does not constitute a performance.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Clarifies that "no restrictions on use" should be understood as "no restrictions on uses not covered by copyright law."
timeline.point_zh: 澄清"无使用限制"应理解为"版权法未涵盖的使用不受限制"。
timeline.point: Clarifies that "no restrictions on use" should be understood as "no restrictions on uses not covered by copyright law."

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Argues by analogy that for software, publishing results of running a program counts as performance and thus use, so imposing conditions on publishing would conflict with the principle of no restrictions on use.
timeline.point_zh: 通过类比论证，运行程序并发布结果属于表演即使用，因此对发布施加条件与禁止限制使用的原则相冲突。
timeline.point: Argues by analogy that for software, publishing results of running a program counts as performance and thus use, so imposing conditions on publishing would conflict with the principle of no restrictions on use.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Hopes someone will explicitly state that the license conforms to the OSD, even if it is not approved.
timeline.point_zh: 希望有人明确判定该许可证符合 OSD，即便不批准。
timeline.point: Hopes someone will explicitly state that the license conforms to the OSD, even if it is not approved.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Acknowledges that restricting performance or publication does constitute a restriction on use.
timeline.point_zh: 承认限制表演/发表确属使用限制。
timeline.point: Acknowledges that restricting performance or publication does constitute a restriction on use.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Clarifies that under US copyright law performance rights do not extend to the execution of software code.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清美国版权法中的表演权不适用于软件代码的执行。
timeline.point: Clarifies that under US copyright law performance rights do not extend to the execution of software code.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Counters that under the WIPO Copyright Treaty and Berne Convention, software as a literary work does carry public performance rights, and cites external deployment clauses in the OSL and RealNetworks licenses.
timeline.point_zh: 反驳认为根据WIPO版权条约和伯尔尼公约，软件作为文学作品确实享有公开表演权，并引用OSL和RealNetworks许可证中的外部部署条款。
timeline.point: Counters that under the WIPO Copyright Treaty and Berne Convention, software as a literary work does carry public performance rights, and cites external deployment clauses in the OSL and RealNetworks licenses.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Skeptical that code execution constitutes public performance, notes agreement with Poole's qualifier, and questions whether license clauses purporting to regulate external deployment actually establish such regulation.
timeline.point_zh: 对代码执行构成公开表演持怀疑态度，同意Poole的限定条件，并质疑许可证中声称规范外部部署的条款是否真正建立了这种规范。
timeline.point: Skeptical that code execution constitutes public performance, notes agreement with Poole's qualifier, and questions whether license clauses purporting to regulate external deployment actually establish such regulation.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Acknowledges imprecise wording and clarifies the intended meaning as "no restrictions on uses not reserved by copyright law," illustrating with an example.
timeline.point_zh: 承认表述不精确，澄清应理解为"版权法未保留的使用不受限制"，并举例说明。
timeline.point: Acknowledges imprecise wording and clarifies the intended meaning as "no restrictions on uses not reserved by copyright law," illustrating with an example.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Academic Citing License
timeline.snippet: Explains that OSL clause 1(d) and clause 5 serve different purposes, and asserts confidence that the external deployment conditions are enforceable as contracts.
timeline.point_zh: 解释OSL第1(d)条和第5条服务于不同目的，并确信外部部署条件作为合同是可执行的。
timeline.point: Explains that OSL clause 1(d) and clause 5 serve different purposes, and asserts confidence that the external deployment conditions are enforceable as contracts.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Submits NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1 for OSI certification, explaining that existing OSI-approved licenses are insufficient because NASA requires government indemnification, U.S. federal law jurisdiction, usage tracking, endorsement restrictions, and mandatory copyleft-style distribution under NOSA.
timeline.point_zh: 提交 NASA 开源协议 1.1 版申请 OSI 认证，说明现有 OSI 批准的许可证不够用，因为 NASA 要求政府免责、美国联邦法律管辖权、使用追踪、背书限制以及强制以 NOSA 进行分发。
timeline.point: Submits NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1 for OSI certification, explaining that existing OSI-approved licenses are insufficient because NASA requires government indemnification, U.S. federal law jurisdiction, usage tracking, endorsement restrictions, and mandatory copyleft-style distribution under NOSA.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Questions each of the five reasons NASA gives for needing a new license, arguing that indemnification, jurisdiction, tracking, endorsement restrictions, and copyleft provisions already exist in approved licenses, and suggests the OSL would meet NASA's needs.
timeline.point_zh: 对 NASA 提出的五项需要新许可证的理由逐一提出质疑，认为免责、管辖权、追踪、背书限制和 copyleft 条款在已批准的许可证中已有先例，建议 OSL 即可满足 NASA 需求。
timeline.point: Questions each of the five reasons NASA gives for needing a new license, arguing that indemnification, jurisdiction, tracking, endorsement restrictions, and copyleft provisions already exist in approved licenses, and suggests the OSL would meet NASA's needs.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Raises numerous questions about the NOSA registration clause, asking whether downloading constitutes "Use" requiring registration, what happens if the registration site is offline, whether the registration is truly voluntary, and why tracking provisions are included in the license at all.
timeline.point_zh: 对 NOSA 注册条款提出大量疑问，包括下载是否构成需要注册的"使用"、注册网站离线怎么办、注册是否真正自愿，以及为什么要在许可证中包含追踪条款。
timeline.point: Raises numerous questions about the NOSA registration clause, asking whether downloading constitutes "Use" requiring registration, what happens if the registration site is offline, whether the registration is truly voluntary, and why tracking provisions are included in the license at all.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Points out that NOSA only requires an "effort to track" rather than actual tracking, and that registration is only "requested" not "required".
timeline.point_zh: 指出 NOSA 只要求"努力追踪"而非实际追踪，且注册只是"请求"而非"要求"。
timeline.point: Points out that NOSA only requires an "effort to track" rather than actual tracking, and that registration is only "requested" not "required".

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Argues that if the intent is merely to show effort, the registration clause should be moved out of the license to avoid confusing non-native English speakers about its legal significance.
timeline.point_zh: 认为如果目的只是展示努力，注册条款应从许可证中移出，以免非英语母语者对其法律意义产生困惑。
timeline.point: Argues that if the intent is merely to show effort, the registration clause should be moved out of the license to avoid confusing non-native English speakers about its legal significance.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Argues the registration clause does not belong in the license itself, as it may deter users who don't want to register or consult a lawyer, and makes the license's open-source status ambiguous.
timeline.point_zh: 认为注册条款不应出现在许可证中，因为它可能阻止不愿注册或咨询律师的用户，并使许可证的开源地位变得模糊。
timeline.point: Argues the registration clause does not belong in the license itself, as it may deter users who don't want to register or consult a lawyer, and makes the license's open-source status ambiguous.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Vigorously defends the NASA license, criticizing critics as "armchair lawyers" who don't respect professional legal drafting, arguing that NASA's lawyers know best and that open-source criteria should not dictate government licensing terms.
timeline.point_zh: 强烈维护 NASA 许可证，批评批评者为"纸上谈兵的律师"，不尊重专业法律起草，认为 NASA 律师最懂行，开源标准不应决定政府许可条款。
timeline.point: Vigorously defends the NASA license, criticizing critics as "armchair lawyers" who don't respect professional legal drafting, arguing that NASA's lawyers know best and that open-source criteria should not dictate government licensing terms.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Corrects Richard Schilling that the mailing list exists to advise OSI on license approval, and clarifies that rejecting tracking requirements is about OSD compliance, not about the license being bad.
timeline.point_zh: 纠正 Richard Schilling 关于邮件列表的用途，明确拒绝追踪要求是关于 OSD 合规性，而非许可证本身的好坏。
timeline.point: Corrects Richard Schilling that the mailing list exists to advise OSI on license approval, and clarifies that rejecting tracking requirements is about OSD compliance, not about the license being bad.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Identifies multiple problems with NOSA: civil servant works cannot be copyrighted under Title 17, the Larger Work provision lacks an aggregation exception potentially violating OSD section 9, the Modification definition is contradictory, the registration clause is inappropriate, the indemnification clause is problematic, and the termination clause discriminates against sublicensees.
timeline.point_zh: 指出 NOSA 的多个问题：公务员作品受 Title 17 限制无法获得版权、Larger Work 条款缺少聚合例外可能违反 OSD 第 9 条、Modification 定义矛盾、注册条款不当、免责条款有问题、终止条款对分许可者构成歧视。
timeline.point: Identifies multiple problems with NOSA: civil servant works cannot be copyrighted under Title 17, the Larger Work provision lacks an aggregation exception potentially violating OSD section 9, the Modification definition is contradictory, the registration clause is inappropriate, the indemnification clause is problematic, and the termination clause discriminates against sublicensees.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: States that the NASA license does not actually require tracking of released software.
timeline.point_zh: 指出 NASA 许可证实际上并不要求追踪已发布的软件。
timeline.point: States that the NASA license does not actually require tracking of released software.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Continues defending the NASA license, arguing that removing indemnification is wrong, that tracking does not make a license non-open-source, and that NASA's license presents an opportunity for OSI to refine its criteria.
timeline.point_zh: 继续维护 NASA 许可证，认为删除免责条款是错误的、追踪不会使许可证变成非开源，并认为 NASA 许可证为 OSI 完善其标准提供了机会。
timeline.point: Continues defending the NASA license, arguing that removing indemnification is wrong, that tracking does not make a license non-open-source, and that NASA's license presents an opportunity for OSI to refine its criteria.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Defends Larry Rosen's review as preliminary and constructive, argues OSD compliance must come first, notes registration requirements have real costs for users without internet access, and questions why NASA wants indemnification without providing it to contributors.
timeline.point_zh: 为 Larry Rosen 的审查辩护称其为初步且建设性的，认为 OSD 合规性必须优先，指出注册要求对无网络的用户有实际成本，并质疑 NASA 要求免责却不向贡献者提供。
timeline.point: Defends Larry Rosen's review as preliminary and constructive, argues OSD compliance must come first, notes registration requirements have real costs for users without internet access, and questions why NASA wants indemnification without providing it to contributors.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Criticizes Larry Rosen's tone toward NASA, argues the indemnification clause does not violate OSD criteria, and proposes that copyright and waivers should not be determinants of open-source status.
timeline.point_zh: 批评 Larry Rosen 对 NASA 的态度，认为免责条款不违反 OSD 标准，并提出版权和免责不应作为开源地位的决定因素。
timeline.point: Criticizes Larry Rosen's tone toward NASA, argues the indemnification clause does not violate OSD criteria, and proposes that copyright and waivers should not be determinants of open-source status.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Explains that license review is an ongoing process of asking questions and suggesting improvements, reminds that quoting private emails is rude, and suspects NOSA will eventually be approved with minor modifications.
timeline.point_zh: 解释许可证审查是一个持续提问和建议改进的过程，提醒引用私人邮件是不礼貌的，并预计 NOSA 最终会经过小幅修改后获批。
timeline.point: Explains that license review is an ongoing process of asking questions and suggesting improvements, reminds that quoting private emails is rude, and suspects NOSA will eventually be approved with minor modifications.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Points out that IPL/CPL section 4 contains an indemnification clause, countering the claim that no OSI-certified license includes one.
timeline.point_zh: 指出 IPL/CPL 第 4 条包含免责条款，反驳了没有 OSI 认证许可证包含免责条款的说法。
timeline.point: Points out that IPL/CPL section 4 contains an indemnification clause, countering the claim that no OSI-certified license includes one.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Questions whether NASA's license is legally coherent, noting that Title 17 prohibits copyright on U.S. government works, which would make the NOSA unnecessary, while also pointing out that transferred copyrights could still be licensable.
timeline.point_zh: 质疑 NASA 许可证在法律上是否自洽，指出 Title 17 禁止对美国政府作品施加版权保护（使 NOSA 不必要），同时指出转让的版权仍可许可。
timeline.point: Questions whether NASA's license is legally coherent, noting that Title 17 prohibits copyright on U.S. government works, which would make the NOSA unnecessary, while also pointing out that transferred copyrights could still be licensable.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Notes that NOSA correctly disclaims copyright for civil servant works within the U.S. but claims copyright outside the U.S., which is a novel and potentially significant legal point.
timeline.point_zh: 指出 NOSA 在美国境内正确地放弃了公务员作品的版权，但在美国境外主张版权，这是一个新颖且潜在重要的法律观点。
timeline.point: Notes that NOSA correctly disclaims copyright for civil servant works within the U.S. but claims copyright outside the U.S., which is a novel and potentially significant legal point.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Explains why tracking requirements are inappropriate in open source licenses: it could make distribution impossible if the tracking organization disappears, prevents anonymous use which violates OSD #5, and contradicts FSF principles.
timeline.point_zh: 解释为什么追踪要求不适合出现在开源许可证中：追踪组织消失可能导致分发不可能、阻止匿名使用违反 OSD #5、且与 FSF 原则相悖。
timeline.point: Explains why tracking requirements are inappropriate in open source licenses: it could make distribution impossible if the tracking organization disappears, prevents anonymous use which violates OSD #5, and contradicts FSF principles.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Rejects the idea that only distribution matters for open-source status, stating the OSD imposes additional requirements, and suggests proposing specific OSD changes if modifications are desired.
timeline.point_zh: 拒绝仅以分发作为开源标准的观点，指出 OSD 有额外要求，并建议如需修改应提出具体的 OSD 变更建议。
timeline.point: Rejects the idea that only distribution matters for open-source status, stating the OSD imposes additional requirements, and suggests proposing specific OSD changes if modifications are desired.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Reiterates confusion about NOSA's legal basis, arguing that Title 17 makes government works public domain everywhere, leaving no copyright to license.
timeline.point_zh: 重申对 NOSA 法律基础的困惑，认为 Title 17 使政府作品在所有地方都进入公共领域，没有可供许可的版权。
timeline.point: Reiterates confusion about NOSA's legal basis, arguing that Title 17 makes government works public domain everywhere, leaving no copyright to license.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Explains that through the Berne Convention, works can be in the public domain in the U.S. but copyrighted elsewhere, and raises the unresolved conflict-of-laws question of whether a work born into the public domain can be copyrighted in another country.
timeline.point_zh: 解释通过《伯尔尼公约》，作品可以在美国进入公共领域但在他国受版权保护，并提出作品在其原产国进入公共领域后能否在他国获得版权的冲突法问题。
timeline.point: Explains that through the Berne Convention, works can be in the public domain in the U.S. but copyrighted elsewhere, and raises the unresolved conflict-of-laws question of whether a work born into the public domain can be copyrighted in another country.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Acknowledges that indemnification clauses exist in other OSI-approved licenses, and while uncomfortable with the broad waiver in NOSA, does not believe it rises to the level of OSD rejection.
timeline.point_zh: 承认免责条款在其他 OSI 批准的许可证中存在，虽然对 NOSA 中的宽泛免责感到不适，但认为不足以构成 OSD 拒绝的理由。
timeline.point: Acknowledges that indemnification clauses exist in other OSI-approved licenses, and while uncomfortable with the broad waiver in NOSA, does not believe it rises to the level of OSD rejection.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Defends usage tracking as beneficial for demonstrating open-source impact to Congress and for product success metrics, argues OSD #5 only prohibits discrimination not tracking, and claims the GNU license's similar requirements are unenforceable.
timeline.point_zh: 为使用追踪辩护，认为其有助于向国会展示开源影响力和衡量产品成功，主张 OSD #5 只禁止歧视而非追踪，并称 GNU 许可证类似要求实际上无法执行。
timeline.point: Defends usage tracking as beneficial for demonstrating open-source impact to Congress and for product success metrics, argues OSD #5 only prohibits discrimination not tracking, and claims the GNU license's similar requirements are unenforceable.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Confirms that under the Berne Convention, a work can be in the public domain in its country of origin but copyrighted elsewhere, citing relevant articles.
timeline.point_zh: 确认根据《伯尔尼公约》，作品可以在其原产国进入公共领域但在他国受版权保护，引用了相关条款。
timeline.point: Confirms that under the Berne Convention, a work can be in the public domain in its country of origin but copyrighted elsewhere, citing relevant articles.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Clarifies that NASA's license requests registration from all recipients (not just direct downloaders), explains the risk if the tracking organization disappears, and corrects the claim that GNU requires submitting changes back to authors.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清 NASA 许可证要求所有接收者注册（不仅是直接下载者），解释追踪组织消失的风险，并纠正 GNU 要求将更改提交回作者的说法。
timeline.point: Clarifies that NASA's license requests registration from all recipients (not just direct downloaders), explains the risk if the tracking organization disappears, and corrects the claim that GNU requires submitting changes back to authors.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Concludes that U.S. government works are in the public domain domestically but copyrighted for 50 years in Australia, meaning Americans can ignore NOSA for civil-servant works but Australians cannot.
timeline.point_zh: 得出结论：美国政府作品在美国境内属公共领域但在澳大利亚受 50 年版权保护，因此美国人可以无视 NOSA 中公务员版本但澳大利亚人不行。
timeline.point: Concludes that U.S. government works are in the public domain domestically but copyrighted for 50 years in Australia, meaning Americans can ignore NOSA for civil-servant works but Australians cannot.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Summarizes three options for NASA's registration clause: (1) move voluntary requests out of the license, (2) stop tricking users if not legally required, or (3) make registration a clear legal requirement, which would likely prevent OSI certification.
timeline.point_zh: 总结 NASA 注册条款的三种选择：（1）将自愿请求移出许可证，（2）如非法律要求则停止误导用户，（3）使注册成为明确的法律要求（但这可能导致无法通过 OSI 认证）。
timeline.point: Summarizes three options for NASA's registration clause: (1) move voluntary requests out of the license, (2) stop tricking users if not legally required, or (3) make registration a clear legal requirement, which would likely prevent OSI certification.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Asks NASA to remove both the tracking clause and the indemnification clause from the license for simplicity, suggesting the tracking request belongs in documentation instead.
timeline.point_zh: 建议 NASA 出于简化目的从许可证中删除追踪条款和免责条款，认为追踪请求应放在文档中。
timeline.point: Asks NASA to remove both the tracking clause and the indemnification clause from the license for simplicity, suggesting the tracking request belongs in documentation instead.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Strongly argues that tracking software usage is fundamentally incompatible with Free/Libre and Open Source Software principles, and warns against OSI weakening the Open Source Definition to accommodate tracking requirements.
timeline.point_zh: 强烈主张追踪软件使用与自由/开源软件原则根本不兼容，并警告 OSI 不应为迁就追踪要求而削弱开源定义。
timeline.point: Strongly argues that tracking software usage is fundamentally incompatible with Free/Libre and Open Source Software principles, and warns against OSI weakening the Open Source Definition to accommodate tracking requirements.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Argues that requiring redistributors to ask users to register is not unreasonable and does not violate the OSD, comparing it to the GPL's requirement to display certain text at startup.
timeline.point_zh: 认为要求分发者请求用户注册并非不合理且不违反 OSD，并将其与 GPL 要求程序启动时显示特定文本进行类比。
timeline.point: Argues that requiring redistributors to ask users to register is not unreasonable and does not violate the OSD, comparing it to the GPL's requirement to display certain text at startup.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Agrees with Russ Nelson that requiring redistributors to ask for registration is acceptable, but notes this falls under the case where NASA should make the legal requirement explicit in the license.
timeline.point_zh: 同意 Russ Nelson 关于要求分发者请求注册是可接受的观点，但指出这属于 NASA 应在许可证中明确法律要求的情况。
timeline.point: Agrees with Russ Nelson that requiring redistributors to ask for registration is acceptable, but notes this falls under the case where NASA should make the legal requirement explicit in the license.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Asks what happens when a US citizen redistributes public domain US Government software in Australia, noting the NOSA will likely fix this jurisdictional issue.
timeline.point_zh: 询问当美国公民在美国公有领域政府软件在澳大利亚重新分发时会发生什么，认为 NOSA 将解决这一管辖权问题。
timeline.point: Asks what happens when a US citizen redistributes public domain US Government software in Australia, noting the NOSA will likely fix this jurisdictional issue.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Points out that NOSA covers patent rights in addition to copyrights, and that the US Government may not have restrictions on patent ownership.
timeline.point_zh: 指出 NOSA 不仅涵盖版权还涵盖专利权，且美国政府在专利所有权方面可能不受限制。
timeline.point: Points out that NOSA covers patent rights in addition to copyrights, and that the US Government may not have restrictions on patent ownership.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Asks whether someone who downloads public domain US Government code via FOIA can relicense it under a BSD license, questioning the right to relicense public domain works.
timeline.point_zh: 询问通过 FOIA 下载公有领域美国政府代码后是否可以将其重新授权为 BSD 许可证，质疑重新授权公有领域作品的权利。
timeline.point: Asks whether someone who downloads public domain US Government code via FOIA can relicense it under a BSD license, questioning the right to relicense public domain works.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Explains that you can do anything with a public domain work except assert valid copyright on it, which is required by BSD and other open-source licenses, so relicensing under BSD is not possible.
timeline.point_zh: 解释对公有领域作品可以做任何事，但不能对其主张有效版权，而 BSD 等开源许可证需要这一权利，因此无法重新授权。
timeline.point: Explains that you can do anything with a public domain work except assert valid copyright on it, which is required by BSD and other open-source licenses, so relicensing under BSD is not possible.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Expresses confusion about whether one can create derivative works of public domain code and release them under a chosen license, such as incorporating PD code into Apache httpd.
timeline.point_zh: 对是否可以创建公有领域代码的衍生作品并以自己选择的许可证发布表示困惑，例如将 PD 代码整合到 Apache httpd 中。
timeline.point: Expresses confusion about whether one can create derivative works of public domain code and release them under a chosen license, such as incorporating PD code into Apache httpd.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Clarifies that creating derivative works of public domain code is allowed, but claiming copyright on the original public domain work itself is not. Raises the follow-up question about extracting public domain parts from a BSD-licensed derivative.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清可以创建公有领域代码的衍生作品，但不能对原始公有领域作品主张版权。提出后续问题：是否可以从 BSD 许可的衍生作品中提取公有领域部分。
timeline.point: Clarifies that creating derivative works of public domain code is allowed, but claiming copyright on the original public domain work itself is not. Raises the follow-up question about extracting public domain parts from a BSD-licensed derivative.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Confirms that creating derivative works of public domain code is allowed, but the derivative work must be genuinely derivative and not just a minor modification.
timeline.point_zh: 确认可以创建公有领域代码的衍生作品，但衍生作品必须是真正的衍生作品，而不仅仅是对原始公有领域代码的轻微修改。
timeline.point: Confirms that creating derivative works of public domain code is allowed, but the derivative work must be genuinely derivative and not just a minor modification.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Agrees that Brian is correct: you can add value to public domain works and license the enhanced version, create derivative works, or simply distribute it better, but the original work remains in the public domain.
timeline.point_zh: 同意 Brian 的观点：可以为公有领域作品增值并许可增强版本、创建衍生作品，或更好地分发原始作品，但原始作品仍处于公有领域。
timeline.point: Agrees that Brian is correct: you can add value to public domain works and license the enhanced version, create derivative works, or simply distribute it better, but the original work remains in the public domain.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Resolves the confusion by confirming both parties are right: nobody can assert copyright on a public domain work itself, but anyone can create a derivative work and license it under any license.
timeline.point_zh: 通过确认双方都正确来解决分歧：没有人可以对公有领域作品本身主张版权，但任何人都可以创建衍生作品并以任何许可证分发。
timeline.point: Resolves the confusion by confirming both parties are right: nobody can assert copyright on a public domain work itself, but anyone can create a derivative work and license it under any license.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Disagrees with John's characterization, arguing that anyone can do anything to a public domain work without a license, and the real question is whether the derivative work has sufficient creativity to be copyrightable.
timeline.point_zh: 不同意 John 的表述，认为任何人都可以对公有领域作品做任何事而无需许可，真正的问题是衍生作品是否具有足够的创造性以获得版权保护。
timeline.point: Disagrees with John's characterization, arguing that anyone can do anything to a public domain work without a license, and the real question is whether the derivative work has sufficient creativity to be copyrightable.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Agrees that the degree of creativity matters, and clarifies that while one cannot fraudulently claim copyright on unmodified public domain code, one can create a genuinely derivative work and apply one's own copyright and license to it.

   released with a license that requires disclosure of source code
   (ex: the GPL).

LIABLE FOR ANY DIRECT, INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, OR
CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES (INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, PROCUREMENT OF
SUBSTITUTE GOODS OR SERVICES; LOSS OF USE, DATA, OR PROFITS; OR
BUSINESS INTERRUPTION) HOWEVER CAUSED AND ON ANY THEORY OF LIABILITY,
WHETHER IN CONTRACT, STRICT LIABILITY, OR TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE
OR OTHERWISE) ARISING IN ANY WAY OUT OF THE USE OF THIS SOFTWARE, EVEN
IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGE.
### END TEMPLATE ###


DISCUSSION:


    The Open Source Software Alliance (hereafter known as "OSSAL"), is
designed to be a business friendly Open Source Software license that
encourages businesses to release or make use of OSSAL software (OSSAL
is a BSDL-like license).  The intent of OSSAL is akin to the phrase,
"if you scratch my back, I'll scratch your back."  With OSSAL
software, a business is able to use and incorporate existing software
that is licensed under the OSSAL or other BSDL-like licenses.  The
incorporated software can be sold.  A business can lend resources to
an OSSAL project and not waive its right to make money from the
software.  By allowing other businesses to have access to non-trade
secret software under the terms of the OSSAL, other businesses can
invest in improving the software.  Both businesses win by
collaborating.  If a business keeps the changes in house and does not
contribute them back to the project, the business incurs a reoccurring
cost for maintaining that software.  The joint nature of OSSAL
software reduces maintenance costs of software.  The extra engineers
and eyes inspecting the code will increase the quality of the code in
terms of functionality and reduce the number of bugs.  OSSAL is
software reciprocity.

    If a business invests in software released under the terms of the GPL
(or a GPL-like license), the money that the business invested into
developing the software is unrecoverable because the software that was
the target of the investment is not commercially viable to the
business that invested in the development effort[1].  The exception to
the software's viability is being able to provide support or
documentation for the software.  If a business manager or engineer
realizes this, one of two things will happen: 1) he or she is going to
dedicate as little resources as possible into solving the problem
because work on GPL software has zero return on investment outside of
satisfying a business's immediate needs, or 2) he or she is going to
realize that it is of no consequence to the business if the quality of
the investment is high or low, therefore they are going to err on the
side of providing a lower quality, less well thought out solution
because it could drive documentation sales or support contracts.

    As for software quality, if the theories of capitalism are true, and
the job market is a functioning market place (the higher the skilled
engineer, the more the engineer is paid.  The more the engineer is
paid, the busier the engineer is.  The more complex product generates
more income and consumes more engineering resources of increasing
skill, thus depriving the open source community of the talents of a
skilled engineer), then businesses with the most qualified engineers
are not working on any percentage of Open Source software.  By
allowing engineers to work on software that is usable by their
business, the quality of the tools of the product that the business
produces, will go up.  By Open Sourcing non-trade secret software
under the OSSAL license, it is now possible, and very potentially
likely that other businesses will invest resources into improving the
OSSAL software.  The corollary to the above statement is that the most
expendable, unimportant engineers work on GPL software and the better
software engineers work on BSDL-licensed software.

    The goal of this license is to promote businesses to open source
non-trade secret software and to contribute resources, when necessary,
to OSSAL or BSDL licensed software.  With multiple businesses using
and working on necessary bug fixes, updates, etc.: the cost of
software development, maintenance, and support goes down; the number
of bugs goes down, and; the quality of the software and its
documentation goes up.  OSSAL also discourages the use of GPL or viral
licenses as they indirectly promote lower quality software that is
widely disseminated, but not reviewed by the more highly skilled
software engineers.  By getting a group of businesses to use and
dedicate resources to OSSAL software, the group of businesses have
created an off the books, informal alliance to help one another.  "If
you scratch my back, I'll scratch yours."
  


FOOTNOTES:


  [1] The GPL requires free availability of the source code for a
product (can only charge for shipping and the material cost of the CD,
disks, etc.), requires that the recipient of the code be bound by the
GPL as well, and requires that any product that uses GPL code, also be
bound to the terms of the GPL (requiring it to be open source and
distributed free of charge if the product is sold).


DOWNLOADS:
An HTML copy of the license can be found at: http://people.FreeBSD.org/~seanc/ossal/ossal.html


COMMENTS, QUESTIONS, and DISCUSSION
If you have any comments, questions, concerns, or would like to discuss this license, please direct them to "Sean Chittenden <sean at chittenden.org>.

that is licensed under the OSSAL or other BSDL-like licenses.  The
incorporated software can be sold.  A business can lend resources to
an OSSAL project and not waive its right to make money from the
software.  By allowing other businesses to have access to non-trade
secret software under the terms of the OSSAL, other businesses can
invest in improving the software.  Both businesses win by
collaborating.  If a business keeps the changes in house and does not
contribute them back to the project, the business incurs a reoccurring
cost for maintaining that software.  The joint nature of OSSAL
software reduces maintenance costs of software.  The extra engineers
and eyes inspecting the code will increase the quality of the code in
terms of functionality and reduce the number of bugs.  OSSAL is
software reciprocity.

viability is being able to provide support or documentation for the
software.  If a business manager or engineer realizes this, one of two
things will happen: 1) he or she is going to dedicate as little
resources as possible into solving the problem because work on GPL
software has zero return on investment outside of satisfying a
business's immediate needs, or 2) he or she is going to realize that
it is of no consequence to the business if the quality of the
investment is high or low, therefore they are going to err on the side
of providing a lower quality, less well thought out solution because
it could drive documentation sales or support contracts.

true, and the job market is a functioning market place (the higher the
skilled engineer, the more the engineer is paid.  The more the
engineer is paid, the busier the engineer is.  The more complex
product generates more income and consumes more engineering resources
of increasing skill, thus depriving the open source community of the
talents of a skilled engineer), then businesses with the most
qualified engineers are not working on any percentage of Open Source
software.  By allowing engineers to work on software that is usable by
their business, the quality of the tools of the product that the
business produces, will go up.  By Open Sourcing non-trade secret
software under the OSSAL license, it is now possible, and very
potentially likely that other businesses will invest resources into
improving the OSSAL software.  The corollary to the above statement is
that the most expendable, unimportant engineers work on GPL software
and the better software engineers work on BSDL-licensed software.

businesses using and working on necessary bug fixes, updates, etc.:

the number of bugs goes down, and; the quality of the software and its
documentation goes up.  OSSAL also discourages the use of GPL or viral
licenses as they indirectly promote lower quality software that is
widely disseminated, but not reviewed by the more highly skilled
software engineers.  By getting a group of businesses to use and
dedicate resources to OSSAL software, the group of businesses have
created an off the books, informal alliance to help one another.  "If
you scratch my back, I'll scratch yours."

source code for a product (can only charge for shipping and the

DISCUSSION:
The Open Source Software Alliance (hereafter known as "OSSAL"), is
designed to be a business friendly Open Source Software license that
encourages businesses to release or make use of OSSAL software (OSSAL
is a BSDL-like license).  The intent of OSSAL is akin to the phrase,
"if you scratch my back, I'll scratch your back."  With OSSAL
software, a business is able to use and incorporate existing software
that is licensed under the OSSAL or other BSDL-like licenses.  The
incorporated software can be sold.  A business can lend resources to
an OSSAL project and not waive its right to make money from the
software.  By allowing other businesses to have access to non-trade
secret software under the terms of the OSSAL, other businesses can
invest in improving the software.  Both businesses win by
collaborating.  If a business keeps the changes in house and does not
contribute them back to the project, the business incurs a reoccurring
cost for maintaining that software.  The joint nature of OSSAL
software reduces maintenance costs of software.  The extra engineers
and eyes inspecting the code will increase the quality of the code in
terms of functionality and reduce the number of bugs.  OSSAL is
software reciprocity.
If a business invests in software released under the terms of the GPL
(or a GPL-like license), the money that the business invested into
developing the software is unrecoverable because the software that was
the target of the investment is not commercially viable to the
business that invested in the development effort[1].  The exception to
the software's viability is being able to provide support or
documentation for the software.  If a business manager or engineer
realizes this, one of two things will happen: 1) he or she is going to
dedicate as little resources as possible into solving the problem
because work on GPL software has zero return on investment outside of
satisfying a business's immediate needs, or 2) he or she is going to
realize that it is of no consequence to the business if the quality of
the investment is high or low, therefore they are going to err on the
side of providing a lower quality, less well thought out solution
because it could drive documentation sales or support contracts.
As for software quality, if the theories of capitalism are true, and
the job market is a functioning market place (the higher the skilled
engineer, the more the engineer is paid.  The more the engineer is
paid, the busier the engineer is.  The more complex product generates
more income and consumes more engineering resources of increasing
skill, thus depriving the open source community of the talents of a
skilled engineer), then businesses with the most qualified engineers
are not working on any percentage of Open Source software.  By
allowing engineers to work on software that is usable by their
business, the quality of the tools of the product that the business
produces, will go up.  By Open Sourcing non-trade secret software
under the OSSAL license, it is now possible, and very potentially
likely that other businesses will invest resources into improving the
OSSAL software.  The corollary to the above statement is that the most
expendable, unimportant engineers work on GPL software and the better
software engineers work on BSDL-licensed software.
The goal of this license is to promote businesses to open source
non-trade secret software and to contribute resources, when necessary,
to OSSAL or BSDL licensed software.  With multiple businesses using
and working on necessary bug fixes, updates, etc.: the cost of
software development, maintenance, and support goes down; the number
of bugs goes down, and; the quality of the software and its
documentation goes up.  OSSAL also discourages the use of GPL or viral
licenses as they indirectly promote lower quality software that is
widely disseminated, but not reviewed by the more highly skilled
software engineers.  By getting a group of businesses to use and
dedicate resources to OSSAL software, the group of businesses have
created an off the books, informal alliance to help one another.  "If
you scratch my back, I'll scratch yours."
FOOTNOTES:
[1] The GPL requires free availability of the source code for a
product (can only charge for shipping and the material cost of the CD,
disks, etc.), requires that the recipient of the code be bound by the
GPL as well, and requires that any product that uses GPL code, also be
bound to the terms of the GPL (requiring it to be open source and
distributed free of charge if the product is sold).

An HTML copy of the license can be found at: http://people.FreeBSD.org/~seanc/ossal/ossal.html
