submissions.name: qmail License

curated_rwp.rejection_reason: Never approved. qmail's license (by Daniel Bernstein) had distribution restrictions that violated OSD.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Argues that the OSD clause is flawed and that qmail should still qualify as open source.
timeline.point_zh: 主张 OSD 条款有缺陷，而 qmail 仍应被视为开源。
timeline.point: Argues that the OSD clause is flawed and that qmail should still qualify as open source.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Acknowledges possible technical workarounds but ultimately rejects qmail's restrictive distribution terms.
timeline.point_zh: 承认可以用工具绕开部分限制，但最终仍否定 qmail 的发行限制。
timeline.point: Acknowledges possible technical workarounds but ultimately rejects qmail's restrictive distribution terms.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Says qmail may allow forking in theory but still raises doubts about whether it satisfies OSD clause 4.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 qmail 在理论上允许分叉，但仍对其是否满足 OSD 第 4 条表示怀疑。
timeline.point: Says qmail may allow forking in theory but still raises doubts about whether it satisfies OSD clause 4.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Clarifies that qmail permits some older binary distributions and that the page's date limits are not the whole story.
timeline.point_zh: 说明 qmail 允许分发某些旧版二进制，页面上的日期限制并不是全部含义。
timeline.point: Clarifies that qmail permits some older binary distributions and that the page's date limits are not the whole story.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Argues that patch-based workflows still permit forking and that the OSD should focus on practical freedom, including binaries.
timeline.point_zh: 主张补丁式流程仍然可以分叉，OSD 应关注实际自由，包括二进制分发。
timeline.point: Argues that patch-based workflows still permit forking and that the OSD should focus on practical freedom, including binaries.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Defends sharing patches but says the OSD still does not clearly require binary distribution rights.
timeline.point_zh: 为补丁分享辩护，但认为 OSD 仍未清楚要求必须允许二进制分发。
timeline.point: Defends sharing patches but says the OSD still does not clearly require binary distribution rights.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Says qmail-style workarounds are awkward and does not treat privileged participation as a problem in itself.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 qmail 式绕行会带来很多别扭边角问题，但并不把特权参与本身视为问题。
timeline.point: Says qmail-style workarounds are awkward and does not treat privileged participation as a problem in itself.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Says qmail-style patch sharing is not enough for the spirit of open source because binaries matter too.
timeline.point_zh: 认为仅靠补丁分享不足以体现开源精神，因为二进制分发同样重要。
timeline.point: Says qmail-style patch sharing is not enough for the spirit of open source because binaries matter too.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Defends qmail's restrictions as compatible with open source and asks for real-world examples of failure.
timeline.point_zh: 为 qmail 的限制辩护，认为它仍可算开源，并要求举出失败的现实例子。
timeline.point: Defends qmail's restrictions as compatible with open source and asks for real-world examples of failure.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Rejects the claim that qmail's conditions are acceptable because they are still not an explicit permission to distribute modified builds.
timeline.point_zh: 否认 qmail 条件可接受，认为它并未明确允许分发由修改源代码构建的软件。
timeline.point: Rejects the claim that qmail's conditions are acceptable because they are still not an explicit permission to distribute modified builds.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Argues that qmail should count because it allows binaries under conditions, even if source releases are constrained.
timeline.point_zh: 主张 qmail 应算合格，因为它在一定条件下允许二进制分发，尽管源码发布受限。
timeline.point: Argues that qmail should count because it allows binaries under conditions, even if source releases are constrained.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Concludes that the qmail page does not satisfy OSD clause 4 because it does not truly allow binaries from modified source.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 qmail 页面并不满足 OSD 第 4 条，因为它并未真正允许由修改源码生成的二进制分发。
timeline.point: Concludes that the qmail page does not satisfy OSD clause 4 because it does not truly allow binaries from modified source.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Says qmail's binary restrictions violate OSD clause 4 if the words are read in their ordinary sense.
timeline.point_zh: 认为如果按通常含义理解，qmail 的二进制限制违反了 OSD 第 4 条。
timeline.point: Says qmail's binary restrictions violate OSD clause 4 if the words are read in their ordinary sense.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Argues that conditional permission can be so restrictive that it does not count as real permission.
timeline.point_zh: 主张附条件的许可可能过于苛刻，因此不算真正的许可。
timeline.point: Argues that conditional permission can be so restrictive that it does not count as real permission.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Rejects qmail's conditional distribution terms as insufficiently permissive under the OSD.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 qmail 的附条件分发条款不足以满足 OSD 要求。
timeline.point: Rejects qmail's conditional distribution terms as insufficiently permissive under the OSD.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Uses a bug-fix example to argue that qmail still allows modified binaries to be redistributed under its conditions.
timeline.point_zh: 用修复 bug 的例子说明 qmail 仍允许在其条件下重新分发修改后的二进制。
timeline.point: Uses a bug-fix example to argue that qmail still allows modified binaries to be redistributed under its conditions.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Notes that all licenses impose conditions, so qmail's use of conditions is not unusual by itself.
timeline.point_zh: 指出所有许可证都会附带条件，因此 qmail 使用条件并不罕见。
timeline.point: Notes that all licenses impose conditions, so qmail's use of conditions is not unusual by itself.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Argues that GPL-style redistribution conditions do not violate the letter of the OSD, but says licenses that block practical forking are not consistent with Open Source values.
timeline.point_zh: 主张 GPL 式的再发行条件并不违反 OSD 的字面含义，但认为阻碍实际分叉的许可证与开源价值不一致。
timeline.point: Argues that GPL-style redistribution conditions do not violate the letter of the OSD, but says licenses that block practical forking are not consistent with Open Source values.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Frames open source as a positive permission to share rather than a control mechanism.
timeline.point_zh: 把开源定义为允许分享的正向许可，而不是控制机制。
timeline.point: Frames open source as a positive permission to share rather than a control mechanism.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Counters that fixing a core-dumping qmail build does change behavior, so the modified version is not equivalent to the original.
timeline.point_zh: 反驳说，修复会崩溃的 qmail 构建会改变行为，因此修改版并不等同于原版。
timeline.point: Counters that fixing a core-dumping qmail build does change behavior, so the modified version is not equivalent to the original.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Argues that OSD clause 3 means a derived qmail build may not be redistributed on the original terms, while welcoming edge-case discussion.
timeline.point_zh: 主张 OSD 第 3 条意味着 qmail 的衍生构建不能按原条款再分发，同时欢迎讨论边界情况。
timeline.point: Argues that OSD clause 3 means a derived qmail build may not be redistributed on the original terms, while welcoming edge-case discussion.

timeline.subject: [License-review] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Suggests waiting for a legal opinion before iterating further, since the license addresses novel legal territory.
timeline.point_zh: 建议在进一步迭代前等待法律意见，因为该许可证涉及新的法律领域。

timeline.subject: [License-review] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Argues the proposal needs legal review before community debate, citing substantial questions under OSD #3, #7, and #10 and the difficulty of imposing copyright-derived conditions on code that may lack copyright.
timeline.point_zh: 认为提案在社区讨论前需要法律审查，引用OSD第3、7、10条的重大问题以及对可能缺乏版权的代码施加版权衍生条件的困难。
timeline.point: Argues the proposal needs legal review before community debate, citing substantial questions under OSD #3, #7, and #10 and the difficulty of imposing copyright-derived conditions on code that may lack copyright.

timeline.subject: [License-review] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Criticizes the proposal for overreading Thaler and for treating file-level labels as reliable authorship boundaries, arguing the threshold legal questions about authorship and enforceability must be resolved first and recommending the proposal move to license-discuss.
timeline.point_zh: 批评提案过度解读Thaler案并将文件级标签视为可靠的作者边界，认为关于作者身份和可执行性的基础法律问题须优先解决，并建议将提案移至license-discuss。
timeline.point: Criticizes the proposal for overreading Thaler and for treating file-level labels as reliable authorship boundaries, arguing the threshold legal questions about authorship and enforceability must be resolved first and recommending the proposal move to license-discuss.

timeline.subject: [License-review] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Notes the submission text appears substantially AI-generated and warns this may invite closer scrutiny and increase the chance of rejection, while acknowledging AI use does not itself violate OSI rules.
timeline.point_zh: 指出提交文本看起来大部分由AI生成，并警告这可能招致更严格的审查并增加被拒绝的风险，同时承认使用AI本身不违反OSI规则。
timeline.point: Notes the submission text appears substantially AI-generated and warns this may invite closer scrutiny and increase the chance of rejection, while acknowledging AI use does not itself violate OSI rules.

timeline.subject: [License-review] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code

timeline.subject: [License-review] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Argues the license contradicts itself by being AI-authored while prohibiting copyright claims on AI content, concluding it has no legal meaning.
timeline.point_zh: 认为该许可证自相矛盾，由AI撰写却禁止对AI内容主张版权，因此没有法律意义。
timeline.point: Argues the license contradicts itself by being AI-authored while prohibiting copyright claims on AI content, concluding it has no legal meaning.

timeline.subject: [License-review] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Defends file-level attribution as a common, accepted approach in major licenses like Apache 2.0, and challenges critics to propose a better alternative.
timeline.point_zh: 为逐文件署名辩护，认为这是Apache 2.0等主流许可证中常见且被接受的做法，并挑战批评者提出更好的替代方案。
timeline.point: Defends file-level attribution as a common, accepted approach in major licenses like Apache 2.0, and challenges critics to propose a better alternative.

timeline.subject: [License-review] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Clarifies he does not object to file-level notices for documentation, but to using file boundaries to make legal conclusions about copyright status, since authorship often spans files and reflects the broader development process.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清他不反对用于文档的文件级通知，但反对使用文件边界对版权状态做出法律结论，因为作者身份通常跨越文件并反映更广泛的开发过程。
timeline.point: Clarifies he does not object to file-level notices for documentation, but to using file boundaries to make legal conclusions about copyright status, since authorship often spans files and reflects the broader development process.

timeline.subject: [License-review] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Acknowledges the authorship-boundary challenge is real but notes it is not new to AI and that no better coping mechanism exists, since authorship clarity fades as software is modified.
timeline.point_zh: 承认作者边界问题确实存在，但指出这不是AI带来的新问题且尚无更好的应对机制，因为随着软件修改作者身份的清晰度会逐渐消失。
timeline.point: Acknowledges the authorship-boundary challenge is real but notes it is not new to AI and that no better coping mechanism exists, since authorship clarity fades as software is modified.

timeline.subject: [License-review] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Argues that the license's value lies in eliminating ambiguity about AI-generated code's copyright status through a contractually adopted and legally enforceable statement, providing adopters with legal security in their use.
timeline.point_zh: 主张该许可证的价值在于通过合同式声明消除 AI 生成代码版权状态的模糊性，为采用者提供使用上的法律安全感。
timeline.point: Argues that the license's value lies in eliminating ambiguity about AI-generated code's copyright status through a contractually adopted and legally enforceable statement, providing adopters with legal security in their use.

timeline.subject: [License-review] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Suggests that the submitter should not directly modify the license text during review, but should instead withdraw and resubmit, while also waiting for more feedback and considering discussion on the license-discuss list first.
timeline.point_zh: 建议提交者在审查期间不要直接修改许可证文本，而应先撤回、等待更多反馈累积修改，并考虑转到 license-discuss 列表先讨论。
timeline.point: Suggests that the submitter should not directly modify the license text during review, but should instead withdraw and resubmit, while also waiting for more feedback and considering discussion on the license-discuss list first.

timeline.subject: [License-review] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Argues the revised draft is unacceptable and must be rejected: relying on SPDX changes is not an assumption license approval can make, and it fails to resolve the real problem of mixed human/AI authorship within a single file.
timeline.point_zh: 认为修订草案不可接受，必须拒绝：依赖 SPDX 改动不属于许可证审批可假设的前提，且未解决同一文件内人机混合作者身份的实际问题。
timeline.point: Argues the revised draft is unacceptable and must be rejected: relying on SPDX changes is not an assumption license approval can make, and it fails to resolve the real problem of mixed human/AI authorship within a single file.

timeline.subject: [License-review] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Asks for clarification on the argument—whether the license text is uncopyrightable because it was AI-generated—and questions what relevance this has to how the license operates.
timeline.point_zh: 提问澄清对方论点——许可证文本是否因 AI 生成而不可享有版权，并质疑这与许可证运作方式有何关系。
timeline.point: Asks for clarification on the argument—whether the license text is uncopyrightable because it was AI-generated—and questions what relevance this has to how the license operates.

timeline.subject: [License-review] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Defends file-level authorship attribution as limited but better than a single project-level declaration, and notes finer-grained (module/function-level) attribution is not yet practical.
timeline.point_zh: 为文件级作者身份声明辩护，认为其虽有限但优于项目级单点声明，并指出更细粒度（模块/函数级）的归属在实践中尚不可行。
timeline.point: Defends file-level authorship attribution as limited but better than a single project-level declaration, and notes finer-grained (module/function-level) attribution is not yet practical.

timeline.subject: [License-review] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Warns that color highlighting in emails may be lost due to mailing list and client settings, suggesting typographical conventions instead, and expresses doubt about whether it matters whether part of the license is AI-generated.
timeline.point_zh: 提醒邮件中颜色高亮可能丢失应改用排版标记，并表示怀疑该许可证是否部分由 AI 生成这一点是否重要。
timeline.point: Warns that color highlighting in emails may be lost due to mailing list and client settings, suggesting typographical conventions instead, and expresses doubt about whether it matters whether part of the license is AI-generated.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Argues that OSI should not approve licenses specifically targeting AI-generated code, as such code is generally uncopyrightable and needs no license; approval would create harmful precedent and falls outside OSI's mandate.
timeline.point_zh: 主张 OSI 不应批准专门针对 AI 生成代码的许可证，因为此类代码通常无版权、无需许可；批准会形成有害先例，且超出 OSI 职权范围。
timeline.point: Argues that OSI should not approve licenses specifically targeting AI-generated code, as such code is generally uncopyrightable and needs no license; approval would create harmful precedent and falls outside OSI's mandate.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Asks the submitter to clarify whether the submission is for discussion only or formal approval, and explains the respective requirements for each path.
timeline.point_zh: 要求提交者澄清是仅讨论还是正式提交审批，并说明两种路径各自的要求。
timeline.point: Asks the submitter to clarify whether the submission is for discussion only or formal approval, and explains the respective requirements for each path.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Draws an analogy to hardware schematics, which are currently uncopyrightable, to illustrate why setting licensing terms over non-copyrightable subject matter is problematic.
timeline.point_zh: 以硬件原理图当前不可享有版权类比，说明为何对无版权客体设定许可权存在风险。
timeline.point: Draws an analogy to hardware schematics, which are currently uncopyrightable, to illustrate why setting licensing terms over non-copyrightable subject matter is problematic.

timeline.subject: [License-review] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Argues that whether the license text is AI-generated only affects copyright claims over the license itself, and OSI approval does not require the license to be copyrightable.
timeline.point_zh: 认为许可证文本是否由 AI 生成仅影响对其自身的版权主张，OSI 审批并不要求许可证本身可享有版权。
timeline.point: Argues that whether the license text is AI-generated only affects copyright claims over the license itself, and OSI approval does not require the license to be copyrightable.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Agrees with the view that AI-generated code will become uncopyrightable, sharing a related article link, but adds the caveat that ideally the AI should be Open Source AI as defined, and it is too early to tell whether machines can self-maintain generated code.
timeline.point_zh: 认同 AI 生成代码走向无版权的观点并附自己文章链接，但补充前提：最好使用开源定义下的 AI，且目前尚早难断机器能否自维护代码。
timeline.point: Agrees with the view that AI-generated code will become uncopyrightable, sharing a related article link, but adds the caveat that ideally the AI should be Open Source AI as defined, and it is too early to tell whether machines can self-maintain generated code.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Points out significant jurisdictional differences in copyrightability of computer-generated works (e.g., UK CDPA s9(3)), and warns that creating licensing norms around AI code when underlying IP rights lack clarity could be codified into law by courts or legislators.
timeline.point_zh: 指出各法域对计算机生成作品可版权性规定差异（如英国 CDPA 9(3)），并警告在底层 IP 权利尚不清晰时为 AI 代码设定许可规范可能被法院/立法者固化成凭空产生的权利。
timeline.point: Points out significant jurisdictional differences in copyrightability of computer-generated works (e.g., UK CDPA s9(3)), and warns that creating licensing norms around AI code when underlying IP rights lack clarity could be codified into law by courts or legislators.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Believes that across most major jurisdictions, the practical treatment of AI-generated code is broadly similar—copyright attaches only to human creative contribution—and warns that licenses should not pre-determine the legal status of AI-generated portions or impose special notice obligations.
timeline.point_zh: 认为各法域对 AI 代码版权处理结果大致趋同（版权只附着于人类贡献），许可证不应在文本中预先判定 AI 生成部分的法律状态并附加特别通知义务。
timeline.point: Believes that across most major jurisdictions, the practical treatment of AI-generated code is broadly similar—copyright attaches only to human creative contribution—and warns that licenses should not pre-determine the legal status of AI-generated portions or impose special notice obligations.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Highlights two major risks: that informal community norms can be codified into law by courts, and that the community generally overestimates the power of licenses and underestimates the limits of copyright, leading to conflicts with companies and disappointment in court.
timeline.point_zh: 强调两大风险：社区非正式规范会被法院固化为法律，以及社区普遍高估许可证与版权的效力、低估其边界，导致与公司冲突并在法庭上失望。
timeline.point: Highlights two major risks: that informal community norms can be codified into law by courts, and that the community generally overestimates the power of licenses and underestimates the limits of copyright, leading to conflicts with companies and disappointment in court.

timeline.subject: [License-review] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Requests withdrawal of the current submission from license-review, intending to summarize the discussion, revise the draft, and continue the concept on license-discuss before any future formal submission.
timeline.point_zh: 请求从 license-review 撤回当前提交，改为在 license-discuss 继续讨论和迭代后再行正式提交。
timeline.point: Requests withdrawal of the current submission from license-review, intending to summarize the discussion, revise the draft, and continue the concept on license-discuss before any future formal submission.

· Trademark Protection: It includes a no-endorsement clause (like BSD-3-Clause and Apache 2.0) to protect the "QmDeve" organization name and identity from being used to endorse derived products without permission.
· Contributor Clarity: It explicitly states that contributions are licensed under the same terms, clarifying the inbound-outbound contribution process for projects.

We believe this combination—a truly permissive core, coupled with explicit patent and trademark protections—creates a balanced and secure license for modern open-source projects.

6. No Discrimination Against Fields of Endeavor: Yes.
7. Distribution of License: Yes. The license applies automatically to all redistributors.
8. License Must Not Be Specific to a Product: Yes. The license is not tied to a specific product.
9. License Must Not Restrict Other Software: Yes. It does not place restrictions on other software distributed alongside it.
10. License Must Be Technology-Neutral: Yes. The license is not specific to any technology or interface.

We have analyzed this license against the MIT and Apache 2.0 licenses.

· vs. MIT: The QmDeve License 1.0 provides significant additional protections (patent and trademark) that the MIT license lacks, addressing a modern legal concern.
· vs. Apache 2.0: While Apache 2.0 is a comprehensive license, it is longer and more complex. The QmDeve License 1.0 aims for a middle ground—providing similar core protections (patent, trademark) but in a potentially more accessible format. We believe this fills a niche for projects that want stronger legal safeguards than MIT but prefer a different structure than Apache 2.0.

This license text has been drafted with careful consideration of established open-source legal language. (Note: We recommend you add here if you have had it reviewed by a qualified attorney, e.g., "It has been reviewed by [Law Firm Name].")

This license is currently planned for use by projects under the "QmDeve" organization on GitHub. We are seeking OSI approval to ensure its legitimacy and foster wider community adoption.

We welcome feedback from the committee and the community and are prepared to discuss and refine the license text based on your recommendations.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely

license_texts.text:
*Released under the Open Innovation License*

Copyright © // Insert information of license holder

*Version 1, 10th November 2020*

*Copyright © 2020 Stark Drones Corporation*
*Copyright © 2020 Andrew Magdy Kamal*

This project is licensed under the *Open Innovation License*. This means
any code, file, diagrams, data format, or other innovation containing this
license within it can be copied, modified, redistributed, published, or
even used for commercial purposes within the context of this license.
Any code, file, diagrams, data format, or other innovation containing this
license is understood to be fully "AS IS", no claims are made in regards to
safety, security, warranty, usability, or other form of merchantability and
market-readiness. In no events are copyright holders, authors, or
publishers are to be held liable for any claims, damage or results from
usage of what have been licensed under this license.

The context of this license includes: Keeping this original license text
verbatim and permissive notice, as well as the copyright notice included in
any redistribution of said project. Project is defined as what is using
this license. For purposes of context, the copyright notice above version
and year is meant to be modified for whomsoever publishes or releases "any
code, file, diagrams, data format, or other innovation", so that they can
include their information. After modifying, the comment saying "// Insert
information of license holder" which starts with // can be removed. This
current paragraph however, will remain in-tact.

Anybody who releases software under the "Open Innovation License" agrees to
at goodwill, build or release technology for the betterment of humanity not
meant with the intention to harm a human being. They agree to a prima facie
moral duty through consequential deontology to understand that technology
should be within the concept of moral good or outcomes that are morally
right and/or ethical. They agree at goodwill to promote the advancement of
humanity and civilization as a whole. They agree to a sense of
adventurement, edification, and the expansion of the human mind.

Said agreement which is within the last paragraph prior to this sentence is
meant to be taken as a general consensus, but not legally enforceable.
Again for context, the last paragraph which starts with "Anybody" and ends
with "human mind" minus quotations, is outside of the boundaries of being
legally enforceable and within the duties of oneselve's actions. The rest
of the license which includes the copyright notice and its context is
within a legally enforceable context. For secondary context, the rest of
the license refers to anything outside of that said paragraph.

____

*Rationale:*

I wanted to release this license for a variety of different reasons.
Infact, I made many posts in regards to why this license is unique and
valuable, and found many developers willing to adapt this license through
small innovation challenges. The license was made on the basis of promoting
a mission statement on ethical technology within the license as well as not
being specific to only software i.e. files, diagrams, data format or any
other innovation.

We also wanted to make sure that the license is adaptable. Many open source
licenses require you to put tons of header files for compliance. We wanted
to make a license that just requires you to contain the license file in
your directory. While many other open source licenses also do that or
follow in similar footsteps, we weren't able to find one that met all these
unique qualities.

Currently, a big inspiration for this license was the idea of promoting
free and open software as well as a mission statement on ethical
technologies. We found that many of the big tech companies that are hailed
as heroes of open source or doing open source initiatives, built
technologies that are harmful to human activity. A technically non-legally
enforceable mission statement within an enforceable open source license was
the way to go. We also made sure to go out of our way to promote the ideals
of open source and free and redistributive software.

*Distinguish:*

I looked at a variety of different open source licenses. The standard being
MIT, then BSD+Patent, ZLib, CDDL, CPAL, CPL, CAL, BSL, and the AFL license.
I feel like MIT, ZLIB, and the Boost licenses focus on redistribution and
code. Those are the standards. The open patent licenses and other licenses
focus on derived original work. However, none of them tried going to the
same extent I wanted in terms of being specific in regards to data formats
or general consensus and mission. I believe this is an important thing to
take into account.

*Legal review:*

Currently I have submitted this to SPDX as well for review through their
GitHub/Website. However, the review time to get approval and receive SPDX
identifiers can be many months. I submitted in November and decided to
submit to OSI while I wait. As for reviewing the context of language myself
and actual legal review, I have thought out reviews through my own legal
council and self judgement as a researcher familiar with these types of
languages.

*Proliferation category:*

I don't necessarily need to be in a Proliferation category as of now, as
many of the licenses on your site are not in a category. However, I would
eventually want to get into the *Licenses that are popular and widely used
or with strong communities *category.

*Version 1, 10th November 2020*
*Copyright © 2020 Stark Drones Corporation*
*Copyright © 2020 Andrew Magdy Kamal*
This project is licensed under the *Open Innovation License*. This means
any code, file, diagrams, data format, or other innovation containing this
license within it can be copied, modified, redistributed, published, or
even used for commercial purposes within the context of this license.
Any code, file, diagrams, data format, or other innovation containing this
license is understood to be fully "AS IS", no claims are made in regards to
safety, security, warranty, usability, or other form of merchantability and
market-readiness. In no events are copyright holders, authors, or
publishers are to be held liable for any claims, damage or results from
usage of what have been licensed under this license.
The context of this license includes: Keeping this original license text
verbatim and permissive notice, as well as the copyright notice included in
any redistribution of said project. Project is defined as what is using
this license. For purposes of context, the copyright notice above version
and year is meant to be modified for whomsoever publishes or releases "any
code, file, diagrams, data format, or other innovation", so that they can
include their information. After modifying, the comment saying "// Insert
information of license holder" which starts with // can be removed. This
current paragraph however, will remain in-tact.
Anybody who releases software under the "Open Innovation License" agrees to
at goodwill, build or release technology for the betterment of humanity not
meant with the intention to harm a human being. They agree to a prima facie
moral duty through consequential deontology to understand that technology
should be within the concept of moral good or outcomes that are morally
right and/or ethical. They agree at goodwill to promote the advancement of
humanity and civilization as a whole. They agree to a sense of
adventurement, edification, and the expansion of the human mind.
Released under the Open Innovation License
Said agreement which is within the last paragraph prior to this sentence is
meant to be taken as a general consensus, but not legally enforceable.
Again for context, the last paragraph which starts with "Anybody" and ends
with "human mind" minus quotations, is outside of the boundaries of being
legally enforceable and within the duties of oneselve's actions. The rest
of the license which includes the copyright notice and its context is
within a legally enforceable context. For secondary context, the rest of
the license refers to anything outside of that said paragraph.
Copyright © // Insert information of license holder
*Rationale:*
Version 1, 10th November 2020
I wanted to release this license for a variety of different reasons.
Infact, I made many posts in regards to why this license is unique and
valuable, and found many developers willing to adapt this license through
small innovation challenges. The license was made on the basis of promoting
a mission statement on ethical technology within the license as well as not
being specific to only software i.e. files, diagrams, data format or any
other innovation.
Copyright © 2020 Stark Drones Corporation
Copyright © 2020 Andrew Magdy Kamal
We also wanted to make sure that the license is adaptable. Many open source
licenses require you to put tons of header files for compliance. We wanted
to make a license that just requires you to contain the license file in
your directory. While many other open source licenses also do that or
follow in similar footsteps, we weren't able to find one that met all these
unique qualities.

This project is licensed under the Open Innovation License. This means any code, file, diagrams, data format, or other innovation containing this license within it can be copied, modified, redistributed, published, or even used for commercial purposes within the context of this license.
Currently, a big inspiration for this license was the idea of promoting
free and open software as well as a mission statement on ethical
technologies. We found that many of the big tech companies that are hailed
as heroes of open source or doing open source initiatives, built
technologies that are harmful to human activity. A technically non-legally
enforceable mission statement within an enforceable open source license was
the way to go. We also made sure to go out of our way to promote the ideals
of open source and free and redistributive software.
*Distinguish:*

Any code, file, diagrams, data format, or other innovation containing this license is understood to be fully "AS IS", no claims are made in regards to safety, security, warranty, usability, or other form of merchantability and market-readiness. In no events are copyright holders, authors, or publishers are to be held liable for any claims, damage or results from usage of what have been licensed under this license.
I looked at a variety of different open source licenses. The standard being
MIT, then BSD+Patent, ZLib, CDDL, CPAL, CPL, CAL, BSL, and the AFL license.
I feel like MIT, ZLIB, and the Boost licenses focus on redistribution and
code. Those are the standards. The open patent licenses and other licenses
focus on derived original work. However, none of them tried going to the
same extent I wanted in terms of being specific in regards to data formats
or general consensus and mission. I believe this is an important thing to
take into account.
*Legal review:*

The context of this license includes: Keeping this original license text verbatim and permissive notice, as well as the copyright notice included in any redistribution of said project. Project is defined as what is using this license. For purposes of context, the copyright notice above version and year is meant to be modified for whomsoever publishes or releases "any code, file, diagrams, data format, or other innovation", so that they can include their information. After modifying, the comment saying "// Insert information of license holder" which starts with // can be removed. This current paragraph however, will remain in-tact.
Currently I have submitted this to SPDX as well for review through their
GitHub/Website. However, the review time to get approval and receive SPDX
identifiers can be many months. I submitted in November and decided to
submit to OSI while I wait. As for reviewing the context of language myself
and actual legal review, I have thought out reviews through my own legal
council and self judgement as a researcher familiar with these types of
languages.

Anybody who releases software under the "Open Innovation License" agrees to at goodwill, build or release technology for the betterment of humanity not meant with the intention to harm a human being. They agree to a prima facie moral duty through consequential deontology to understand that technology should be within the concept of moral good or outcomes that are morally right and/or ethical. They agree at goodwill to promote the advancement of humanity and civilization as a whole. They agree to a sense of adventurement, edification, and the expansion of the human mind.
*Proliferation category:*

Said agreement which is within the last paragraph prior to this sentence is meant to be taken as a general consensus, but not legally enforceable. Again for context, the last paragraph which starts with "Anybody" and ends with "human mind" minus quotations, is outside of the boundaries of being legally enforceable and within the duties of oneselve's actions. The rest of the license which includes the copyright notice and its context is within a legally enforceable context. For secondary context, the rest of the license refers to anything outside of that said paragraph.
I don't necessarily need to be in a Proliferation category as of now, as
many of the licenses on your site are not in a category. However, I would
eventually want to get into the *Licenses that are popular and widely used
or with strong communities *category.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Submits the Open Innovation License (OIN) for OSI approval, a permissive license with a non-binding ethical mission statement, distinguishing it from existing licenses by covering data formats and embedding ethical principles.
timeline.point_zh: 提交开放创新许可证 (OIN) 申请 OSI 批准，这是一款附带非约束性伦理使命宣言的宽松许可证，通过覆盖数据格式和嵌入伦理原则与现有许可证加以区分。
timeline.point: Submits the Open Innovation License (OIN) for OSI approval, a permissive license with a non-binding ethical mission statement, distinguishing it from existing licenses by covering data formats and embedding ethical principles.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Identifies multiple drafting problems: the grant could be read as restricting to commercial use only, the mission statement uses binding language ('agree') despite being intended as non-binding, and the OIN acronym conflicts with the Open Invention Network trademark.
timeline.point_zh: 指出多处起草问题：授权条款可能被解读为仅限商业用途，使命宣言使用了约束性措辞（'agree'）但意图是非约束性的，且 OIN 缩写与 Open Invention Network 的商标冲突。
timeline.point: Identifies multiple drafting problems: the grant could be read as restricting to commercial use only, the mission statement uses binding language ('agree') despite being intended as non-binding, and the OIN acronym conflicts with the Open Invention Network trademark.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Defends the OIN license against criticism: argues 'or even used for commercial purposes' is permissive not restrictive, the mission statement is explicitly non-binding, and the OIN acronym is not confusing since no other open source license uses it.
timeline.point_zh: 为 OIN 许可证辩护：认为'or even used for commercial purposes'是许可性的而非限制性的，使命宣言明确声明不具约束力，且 OIN 缩写不会造成混淆因为目前没有其他开源许可证使用该缩写。
timeline.point: Defends the OIN license against criticism: argues 'or even used for commercial purposes' is permissive not restrictive, the mission statement is explicitly non-binding, and the OIN acronym is not confusing since no other open source license uses it.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Counters that if the grant of 'use' is interpreted as limited to commercial purposes, it violates the OSD. Sarcastically suggests the submitter skip the review process entirely if the license is so clearly compliant.
timeline.point_zh: 反驳称如果'使用'授权被解读为仅限商业用途，则违反了 OSD。讽刺地建议提交者如果认为许可证如此明确合规，不妨直接跳过审查流程提交董事会投票。
timeline.point: Counters that if the grant of 'use' is interpreted as limited to commercial purposes, it violates the OSD. Sarcastically suggests the submitter skip the review process entirely if the license is so clearly compliant.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Reiterates that 'or even used for commercial purposes' uses 'or' to indicate an additional permitted use, not a restriction, and that 'can be' before the list confirms all items are permissive options.
timeline.point_zh: 重申'or even used for commercial purposes'中的'or'表示额外的许可用途而非限制，列表前的'can be'确认所有选项都是许可性的。
timeline.point: Reiterates that 'or even used for commercial purposes' uses 'or' to indicate an additional permitted use, not a restriction, and that 'can be' before the list confirms all items are permissive options.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Urges the submitter to heed McCoy Smith's legal expertise and seriously consider the drafting issues raised, warning that the license risks rejection if submitted as-is.
timeline.point_zh: 敦促提交者认真听取 McCoy Smith 的法律专业意见，切实考虑所提出的起草问题，警告如果原样提交将面临被拒绝的风险。
timeline.point: Urges the submitter to heed McCoy Smith's legal expertise and seriously consider the drafting issues raised, warning that the license risks rejection if submitted as-is.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Expresses a generally positive view that the license is close to OSD-compliant and that non-legally binding ethical statements can be part of an open source license, but notes the wording could be clearer.
timeline.point_zh: 总体上认为该许可证接近 OSD 合规，非约束性的伦理声明可以作为开源许可证的一部分，但认为措辞可以更清晰。
timeline.point: Expresses a generally positive view that the license is close to OSD-compliant and that non-legally binding ethical statements can be part of an open source license, but notes the wording could be clearer.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Disagrees with McCoy Smith's interpretation of the commercial use clause, arguing that the comma-separated list structure and the word 'even' clearly indicate an additional permitted use, not a restriction.
timeline.point_zh: 不同意 McCoy Smith 对商业使用条款的解读，认为逗号分隔的列表结构和'even'一词清楚表明这是额外的许可用途而非限制。
timeline.point: Disagrees with McCoy Smith's interpretation of the commercial use clause, arguing that the comma-separated list structure and the word 'even' clearly indicate an additional permitted use, not a restriction.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Thanks Eric Schultz for his feedback on the OIN license.
timeline.point_zh: 感谢 Eric Schultz 对 OIN 许可证的反馈。
timeline.point: Thanks Eric Schultz for his feedback on the OIN license.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Identifies the interesting question of whether a non-legally binding ethical use restriction can satisfy the OSD, suggesting the Board may want to address this as precedent even if this particular license is not the best vehicle.
timeline.point_zh: 提出一个有趣的问题：非约束性的伦理使用限制能否满足 OSD，建议董事会可以借此作为先例来回应，即使该许可证本身不是最佳载体。
timeline.point: Identifies the interesting question of whether a non-legally binding ethical use restriction can satisfy the OSD, suggesting the Board may want to address this as precedent even if this particular license is not the best vehicle.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Argues that a non-legally binding ethical statement can coexist with OSD compliance, since the mission statement is explicitly marked as non-binding within the binding license and does not restrict use.
timeline.point_zh: 主张非约束性的伦理声明可以与 OSD 合规共存，因为使命宣言在约束性许可证中被明确标记为不具约束力，且不限制使用。
timeline.point: Argues that a non-legally binding ethical statement can coexist with OSD compliance, since the mission statement is explicitly marked as non-binding within the binding license and does not restrict use.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Provides detailed critique of the OIN license: non-operative language should be removed entirely, the commercial use clause is unnecessary and confusing, and the copyright notices are unclear. Concludes the license offers no benefit over existing well-accepted permissive licenses.
timeline.point_zh: 对 OIN 许可证进行详细批评：无操作性语言应完全删除，商业使用条款不必要且造成混淆，版权声明不清晰。总结认为该许可证相比现有的成熟宽松许可证没有任何优势。
timeline.point: Provides detailed critique of the OIN license: non-operative language should be removed entirely, the commercial use clause is unnecessary and confusing, and the copyright notices are unclear. Concludes the license offers no benefit over existing well-accepted permissive licenses.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Defends the OIN license by explaining the copyright notice parallels other licenses, the commercial use clause explicitly permits both commercial and non-commercial use, and the mission statement serves an inspirational purpose without creating legal obligations.
timeline.point_zh: 为 OIN 许可证辩护：解释版权声明与其他许可证类似，商业使用条款明确允许商业和非商业用途，使命宣言服务于启发目的而不产生法律义务。
timeline.point: Defends the OIN license by explaining the copyright notice parallels other licenses, the commercial use clause explicitly permits both commercial and non-commercial use, and the mission statement serves an inspirational purpose without creating legal obligations.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Reports that the OIN license has been actively adopted by approximately 57 software teams in hackathons and open innovation challenges, with no users reporting confusion about commercial-only usage or the mission statement wording.
timeline.point_zh: 报告 OIN 许可证已被约 57 个软件团队在黑客马拉松和开放创新挑战赛中积极采用，目前没有任何用户反映对仅限商业使用或使命宣言措辞感到困惑。
timeline.point: Reports that the OIN license has been actively adopted by approximately 57 software teams in hackathons and open innovation challenges, with no users reporting confusion about commercial-only usage or the mission statement wording.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Agrees to provide a license-by-license analysis in response to reviewer feedback.
timeline.point_zh: 同意针对审查反馈提供逐许可证分析。
timeline.point: Agrees to provide a license-by-license analysis in response to reviewer feedback.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Defends the use of 'OIN' by arguing 'open innovation' is a generic term used since the 1960s, more people know the term than the organization, and no other open source license uses the OIN identifier.
timeline.point_zh: 为使用'OIN'辩护，认为'open innovation'是自 1960 年代以来使用的通用术语，更多人知道这个术语而非该组织，且目前没有其他开源许可证使用 OIN 标识符。
timeline.point: Defends the use of 'OIN' by arguing 'open innovation' is a generic term used since the 1960s, more people know the term than the organization, and no other open source license uses the OIN identifier.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Argues the OIN license has not demonstrated a use case that existing approved licenses cannot serve, suggests a license-by-license comparison table, and recommends moving the mission statement to a separate manifesto rather than embedding it in the license.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 OIN 许可证未证明其能解决现有已批准许可证无法满足的使用场景，建议制作逐一对比现有许可证的分析表，并推荐将使命宣言移至独立宣言而非嵌入许可证正文中。
timeline.point: Argues the OIN license has not demonstrated a use case that existing approved licenses cannot serve, suggests a license-by-license comparison table, and recommends moving the mission statement to a separate manifesto rather than embedding it in the license.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Warns that using 'OIN' for the license name creates genuine confusion with the Open Invention Network, which operates primarily in the open source space, and suggests finding an alternative name instead of arguing for the current one.
timeline.point_zh: 警告使用'OIN'作为许可证名称会与主要在开源领域运营的 Open Invention Network 产生真正的混淆，建议花精力寻找替代名称而非为当前名称辩护。
timeline.point: Warns that using 'OIN' for the license name creates genuine confusion with the Open Invention Network, which operates primarily in the open source space, and suggests finding an alternative name instead of arguing for the current one.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Points to a live USPTO trademark registration for 'OIN' by Open Invention Network, LLC, and advises the submitter to consult their lawyer about the trademark conflict.
timeline.point_zh: 指向 Open Invention Network, LLC 持有的'OIN'有效 USPTO 商标注册，建议提交者就商标冲突问题咨询律师。
timeline.point: Points to a live USPTO trademark registration for 'OIN' by Open Invention Network, LLC, and advises the submitter to consult their lawyer about the trademark conflict.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Provides the details of the live trademark registration for 'OIN' held by Open Invention Network, LLC, covering licensing of intellectual property and innovation-related services.
timeline.point_zh: 提供了 Open Invention Network, LLC 持有的'OIN'有效商标注册详细信息，涵盖知识产权许可和创新相关服务。
timeline.point: Provides the details of the live trademark registration for 'OIN' held by Open Invention Network, LLC, covering licensing of intellectual property and innovation-related services.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Argues the license is non-free because it imposes moral obligations on distributors that go far beyond the scope of the licensed work and creates burden on people outside the licensing context.
timeline.point_zh: 认为该许可证是非自由的，因为它对分发者施加了超出被许可工作范围的道德义务，并给许可范围之外的人造成了负担。
timeline.point: Argues the license is non-free because it imposes moral obligations on distributors that go far beyond the scope of the licensed work and creates burden on people outside the licensing context.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Notes the trademark at issue is cancelled and IC42 does not cover relevant services; announces acronym change from OIN to OPNL via a GitHub pull request to avoid conflict.
timeline.point_zh: 指出相关商标已被取消且IC42不涵盖相关服务；宣布通过GitHub PR将缩写从OIN改为OPNL以避免冲突。
timeline.point: Notes the trademark at issue is cancelled and IC42 does not cover relevant services; announces acronym change from OIN to OPNL via a GitHub pull request to avoid conflict.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Argues that difficult wording does not violate OSD standards and the license’s moral mission statement is distinct from discriminatory restrictions; plans to submit a license-by-license analysis.
timeline.point_zh: 认为措辞复杂不违反OSD标准，许可证中的道德使命声明与歧视性限制有本质区别；计划提交逐条许可证分析。
timeline.point: Argues that difficult wording does not violate OSD standards and the license’s moral mission statement is distinct from discriminatory restrictions; plans to submit a license-by-license analysis.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Argues the license imposes morally binding requirements on behavior that go far beyond the scope of the licensed work, is thought- or behavior-controlling, and fails OSD compliance; casts a veto.
timeline.point_zh: 认为该许可证对行为施加了超出被许可工作范围的道德约束，试图控制思想或行为，远不符合OSD合规要求；投下反对票。
timeline.point: Argues the license imposes morally binding requirements on behavior that go far beyond the scope of the licensed work, is thought- or behavior-controlling, and fails OSD compliance; casts a veto.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Argues that moral restrictions are different from legal restrictions, the moral bar is very low, and ethical mission statements should not be grounds for OSD rejection; notes most people veto without waiting for his analysis.
timeline.point_zh: 主张道德限制不同于法律限制，道德门槛很低，伦理使命声明不应成为OSD拒绝的理由；指出多数人在未等待其分析之前就投了反对票。
timeline.point: Argues that moral restrictions are different from legal restrictions, the moral bar is very low, and ethical mission statements should not be grounds for OSD rejection; notes most people veto without waiting for his analysis.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Points out that the phrase ‘at goodwill’ is unusual and not found in common usage; asks the submitter to clarify what is intended by that phrase.
timeline.point_zh: 指出‘at goodwill’这一表述不常见且在通用英语中没有使用证据；要求提交者澄清其含义。
timeline.point: Points out that the phrase ‘at goodwill’ is unusual and not found in common usage; asks the submitter to clarify what is intended by that phrase.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Argues that license usage is voluntary, so morality-based arguments should not factor into OSD review; asserts people can judge for themselves whether to accept a mission statement.
timeline.point_zh: 认为许可证使用是自愿的，因此基于道德的论点不应影响OSD审查；主张人们有能力自行判断是否接受使命声明。
timeline.point: Argues that license usage is voluntary, so morality-based arguments should not factor into OSD review; asserts people can judge for themselves whether to accept a mission statement.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Explains that ‘goodwill’ is a philosophical term for acting out of personal responsibility; compares to purpose-specific licenses like Apple 2; argues the license is within OSI boundaries.
timeline.point_zh: 解释‘goodwill’是哲学用语，意为基于个人责任行事；与Apple 2等特定用途许可证类比；认为该许可证仍在OSI范围内。
timeline.point: Explains that ‘goodwill’ is a philosophical term for acting out of personal responsibility; compares to purpose-specific licenses like Apple 2; argues the license is within OSI boundaries.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Argues that requiring a moral promise in a license is a behavior requirement bound to honour, which is not permitted in open source; open source is about minimal strings attached, not adding more.
timeline.point_zh: 认为在许可证中要求道德承诺是对行为的约束，违反了开源原则；开源的核心是尽量少的附加条件，而不是增加更多。
timeline.point: Argues that requiring a moral promise in a license is a behavior requirement bound to honour, which is not permitted in open source; open source is about minimal strings attached, not adding more.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Points out that ‘goodwill’ also has a distinct legal meaning, providing a reference link.
timeline.point_zh: 指出‘goodwill’同时具有独立的法律含义，并提供了参考链接。
timeline.point: Points out that ‘goodwill’ also has a distinct legal meaning, providing a reference link.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Counters that the mission statement is not legally binding, emphasizes personal responsibility with no central authority enforcement, and compares it to codes of conduct and other licenses with restrictive clauses.
timeline.point_zh: 反驳称该使命声明不具法律约束力，强调个人责任且无中央权威强制执行，并与行为准则和其他含有约束条款的许可证进行类比。
timeline.point: Counters that the mission statement is not legally binding, emphasizes personal responsibility with no central authority enforcement, and compares it to codes of conduct and other licenses with restrictive clauses.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Contains no substantive message body in the archived OIN License approval thread.
timeline.point_zh: 在 OIN License 批准线程中没有可提取的实质邮件正文。
timeline.point: Contains no substantive message body in the archived OIN License approval thread.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Clarifies that ‘at goodwill’ differs from ‘goodwill’ alone; the ‘at’ modifier changes the meaning and context is implied by the following text.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清‘at goodwill’与单独的‘goodwill’不同；‘at’修饰语改变了含义，上下文由后续内容暗示。
timeline.point: Clarifies that ‘at goodwill’ differs from ‘goodwill’ alone; the ‘at’ modifier changes the meaning and context is implied by the following text.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Says the name “OIN License” creates obvious confusion with a well-known existing mark; finds the wording lacks rigor and the license does not fill a clear legal niche from a proliferation standpoint.
timeline.point_zh: 认为“OIN许可证”这一名称与知名现有商标明显混淆；指出措辞缺乏严谨性，许可证在增殖角度未能填补明确的法律空白。
timeline.point: Says the name “OIN License” creates obvious confusion with a well-known existing mark; finds the wording lacks rigor and the license does not fill a clear legal niche from a proliferation standpoint.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Argues ethical restrictions on open source are an oxymoron because the recipient, not the creator, decides what is ethical; says this license does not solve a problem the open source community perceives and urges the submitter to withdraw it.
timeline.point_zh: 认为对开源施加伦理限制是矛盾的，因为决定使用是否合乎伦理的是接收者而非创建者；表示该许可证未能解决开源社区所认知的问题，敦促提交者撤回。
timeline.point: Argues ethical restrictions on open source are an oxymoron because the recipient, not the creator, decides what is ethical; says this license does not solve a problem the open source community perceives and urges the submitter to withdraw it.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Recommends retracting the license, reworking the wording with legal counsel to address concerns, and resubmitting rather than pushing back on every objection to the wording.
timeline.point_zh: 建议撤回许可证，与法律顾问合作修改措辞以解决关切，然后重新提交，而不是对每一条措辞反对意见都进行反驳。
timeline.point: Recommends retracting the license, reworking the wording with legal counsel to address concerns, and resubmitting rather than pushing back on every objection to the wording.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Responds to criticism by defending the mission statement as non-binding and voluntary; suggests the issue may be complexity rather than content; is considering a version 2 revision to address concerns and seek OSI approval.
timeline.point_zh: 回应批评，辩护使命声明是非约束性的且自愿的；认为问题可能在于复杂性而非内容本身；正在考虑发布第二版修订以解决关切并寻求OSI批准。
timeline.point: Responds to criticism by defending the mission statement as non-binding and voluntary; suggests the issue may be complexity rather than content; is considering a version 2 revision to address concerns and seek OSI approval.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Asks Andrew to withdraw the current license version to save everyone’s time, noting that no one supports this version and its chances of approval are slim.
timeline.point_zh: 要求Andrew撤回当前许可证版本以节省大家的时间，指出没有人支持该版本且获批希望渺茫。
timeline.point: Asks Andrew to withdraw the current license version to save everyone’s time, noting that no one supports this version and its chances of approval are slim.

timeline.subject: [License-review] Approval: OIN License (Open Innovation License)
timeline.snippet: Provides the permanent USPTO TSDR link for the OIN trademark registration record.
timeline.point_zh: 提供了OIN商标注册记录的USPTO TSDR永久链接。
timeline.point: Provides the permanent USPTO TSDR link for the OIN trademark registration record.
