- *Part one: The existing OSI-approved license that is most similar to
CeCILL: *

* *

Since 2005, the GNU GPL stays the most similar OSI approved license to
CeCILL. The publication of the GPL license v.3 doesn’t change the
similarity between the 2 licenses.



Nevertheless, since 2005, we have noted 2 others licenses similar to
CeCILL:

-       The Affero GPL license v.3

-       The EUPL v.1.1.



As CeCILL license, all these licenses have the same aim of maintaining the
distribution of software, including modified software, under the same or
similar open source license. These similarities are on the principles: from
a legal point of view, CeCILL license v.2.1 is really different.


*Why this license was not sufficient for our needs: *



At first, these licenses don’t clearly refer to an applicable law. We
believe that it’s as necessary for open source licenses to refer to an
applicable law as for others type of agreements because it reduces legal
uncertainties for companies: in case of litigation, the dispute can be
easily analyzed by lawyers and companies don’t have to wait for the judge
decision to know which the applicable law is.



Moreover, theses licenses are not, in our opinion, sufficiently clear on
developments which shall be keep under the same license:

-       In GPL v.3 and Affero GPL v.3 the difference between the covered
works and an aggregate is not simple to understand in all cases *(“**A
compilation of a covered work with other separate and independent works,
which are not by their nature extensions of the covered work, and which are
not combined with it such as to form a larger program, in or on a volume of
a storage or distribution medium, is called an “aggregate” if the
compilation and its resulting copyright are not used to limit the access or
legal rights of the compilation's users beyond what the individual works
permit. Inclusion of a covered work in an aggregate does not cause this
License to apply to the other parts of the aggregate.”)*;

-       the “derivatives works” in the EUPL v.1.1 are defined as *“the
works or software that could be created by the Licensee, based upon the
Original Work or modifications thereof. This Licence does not define the
extent of modification or dependence on the Original Work required in order
to classify a work as a Derivative Work; this extent is determined by
copyright law applicable in the country mentioned in Article 15”*. This
definition undertakes users to search themselves for each software program
distributed under EUPL v.1.1 which is the applicable law and, in this law,
which is the meaning of a derivative work.



Furthermore in terms of compatibility, the EUPL doesn’t include the GNU
GPL v3 on its compatibility clause list having these two licenses
“copyleft” provisions in conflict.



However, CeCILL includes a provision that allows the distribution of its
code within code covered by GNU GPL, making it explicitly compatible with
any version of the GNU GPL including the v3.



We also believe that CeciLL covers many details of software law, such as
the right to translate,  provides efficient and detailed provisions about
using rights, distribution rights, warranties and responsibility.



CeciLL also provides a satisfying solution to issues on moral rights of
the authors and compatibility with other licenses.



According to these developments, we believe that CeCILL is safer from a
legal point of view.


- *Part two: How software distributed under your license can be used in
conjunction with software distributed under other open source licenses:*



Software distributed under CeCILL license v.2.1 can be used freely with
other open source licenses. This license contains no restrictions as to
possible use together with other software.
CeCILL provides, since its version 2.0, a special exception for the GPL
license. In its version 2.1, we add another special exception: when a work
covered by CeCILL is combined with a work covered by Affero GPL, the Affero
GPL takes precedence (see clause 5.3.4 of CeCILL).



*Software licenses that are entirely incompatible with CeCILL:*


Any software licenses that are entirely incompatible with the GNU GPL.


*- Part three: *the plain text of CeCILL v.2.1 follows.





Concerning the three criteria here is our analysis:



*1. The license must not be duplicative*

* *

CeCILL v.2.1 retains the principles of the GNU GPL but it cannot be seen
as duplicative for the following reasons. We believe that CeCILL is worth
adding as an Open Source license because it addresses the corresponding
problems not addressed by the GPL: better and safer legal foundation (at
least in Europe), better protection of the programmer and clearer
mechanisms:

- from a legal point of view, at least by referring to a specific law,
CeCILL is very different. Moreover, the liability clause of CeCILL is
taking into account consumer's rights effectively to provide the minimum
level of liability for the programmer

- for developers, the notions of "covered work" and “aggregate” are
different than the mechanism of “external modules” and “internal modules”
more flexible.  With CeCILL, the programmer can choose to develop an
internal module if he wants to distribute its development under CeCILL but
he still has the choice to develop an external module if he prefers to
choose another license for this module.



To elaborate more on the better legal safety:

- The mention of a (reasonable) applicable law considerably reduces the
risk of having a judge declare some provisions of the license invalid or
interpret some provisions differently from the intent of the authors of the
license. The Munich court that examined in 2004 the GPL determined that
German law should apply but nevertheless was not able to tell whether some
clauses of the GPL are really valid or not (according to the German
Copyright Act). That examplifies legal risks of the GPL, at least in Europe.

Even if CeCILL is submitted to the French Law, it  was written to be
conformant to the relevant European directives and regulations (directive
on the legal protection of computer programs, directive on unfair terms in
consumer contracts, directive on the approximation of the laws, regulations
and administrative provisions of the Member States concerning liability for
defective products, convention on the law applicable to contractual
obligations, and regulation on jurisdiction and the recognition and
enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters). That makes it as
close as possible to what a multinational (European) license can be now.



2. The license must be clearly written, simple, and understandable.



Although CeCILL has been written and reviewed by lawyers, it has been
designed to be read and understood by a programmer (computer scientists and
software engineers were indeed part of the team that wrote the license).
Note that although the text of CeCILL is significantly longer than the text
of other Open Source licenses, we believe that it makes CeCILL much clearer
than most shorter licenses.



We now have more than 6 years experience with the version 2 of CeCILL that
has been debated by various non legal Open Source Software users and we
collected a lot of feedback from programmers.

As recommended by OSI board in 2005, we choose to modify articles 5.3.1
and 5.3.2 of CeCILL v.2.1 in order to clarify the obligation of the
licensee to allow access to the source code in the event that only the
object code of the software is redistributed. CeCILL v.2.1 provides that:

-       the Licensee undertakes to allow effective access to the full
source code of the software,

-       this obligation is limited in time : at least 3 years from the
distribution of the modified software.





3. The license must be reusable.



CeCILL is clearly reusable (it has not been designed for a specific
Program or specific licensees or licensors)

- *Part one: The existing OSI-approved license that is most similar to
CeCILL: *

* *

Since 2005, the GNU GPL stays the most similar OSI approved license to
CeCILL. The publication of the GPL license v.3 doesn’t change the
similarity between the 2 licenses.



Nevertheless, since 2005, we have noted 2 others licenses similar to
CeCILL:

-       The Affero GPL license v.3

-       The EUPL v.1.1.



As CeCILL license, all these licenses have the same aim of maintaining the
distribution of software, including modified software, under the same or
similar open source license. These similarities are on the principles: from
a legal point of view, CeCILL license v.2.1 is really different.


*Why this license was not sufficient for our needs: *



At first, these licenses don’t clearly refer to an applicable law. We
believe that it’s as necessary for open source licenses to refer to an
applicable law as for others type of agreements because it reduces legal
uncertainties for companies: in case of litigation, the dispute can be
easily analyzed by lawyers and companies don’t have to wait for the judge
decision to know which the applicable law is.



Moreover, theses licenses are not, in our opinion, sufficiently clear on
developments which shall be keep under the same license:

-       In GPL v.3 and Affero GPL v.3 the difference between the covered
works and an aggregate is not simple to understand in all cases *(“**A
compilation of a covered work with other separate and independent works,
which are not by their nature extensions of the covered work, and which are
not combined with it such as to form a larger program, in or on a volume of
a storage or distribution medium, is called an “aggregate” if the
compilation and its resulting copyright are not used to limit the access or
legal rights of the compilation's users beyond what the individual works
permit. Inclusion of a covered work in an aggregate does not cause this
License to apply to the other parts of the aggregate.”)*;

-       the “derivatives works” in the EUPL v.1.1 are defined as *“the
works or software that could be created by the Licensee, based upon the
Original Work or modifications thereof. This Licence does not define the
extent of modification or dependence on the Original Work required in order
to classify a work as a Derivative Work; this extent is determined by
copyright law applicable in the country mentioned in Article 15”*. This
definition undertakes users to search themselves for each software program
distributed under EUPL v.1.1 which is the applicable law and, in this law,
which is the meaning of a derivative work.



Furthermore in terms of compatibility, the EUPL doesn’t include the GNU
GPL v3 on its compatibility clause list having these two licenses
“copyleft” provisions in conflict.



However, CeCILL includes a provision that allows the distribution of its
code within code covered by GNU GPL, making it explicitly compatible with
any version of the GNU GPL including the v3.



We also believe that CeciLL covers many details of software law, such as
the right to translate,  provides efficient and detailed provisions about
using rights, distribution rights, warranties and responsibility.



CeciLL also provides a satisfying solution to issues on moral rights of
the authors and compatibility with other licenses.



According to these developments, we believe that CeCILL is safer from a
legal point of view.


- *Part two: How software distributed under your license can be used in
conjunction with software distributed under other open source licenses:*



Software distributed under CeCILL license v.2.1 can be used freely with
other open source licenses. This license contains no restrictions as to
possible use together with other software.
CeCILL provides, since its version 2.0, a special exception for the GPL
license. In its version 2.1, we add another special exception: when a work
covered by CeCILL is combined with a work covered by Affero GPL, the Affero
GPL takes precedence (see clause 5.3.4 of CeCILL).



*Software licenses that are entirely incompatible with CeCILL:*


Any software licenses that are entirely incompatible with the GNU GPL.


*- Part three: *the plain text of CeCILL v.2.1 follows.





Concerning the three criteria here is our analysis:



*1. The license must not be duplicative*

* *

CeCILL v.2.1 retains the principles of the GNU GPL but it cannot be seen
as duplicative for the following reasons. We believe that CeCILL is worth
adding as an Open Source license because it addresses the corresponding
problems not addressed by the GPL: better and safer legal foundation (at
least in Europe), better protection of the programmer and clearer
mechanisms:

- from a legal point of view, at least by referring to a specific law,
CeCILL is very different. Moreover, the liability clause of CeCILL is
taking into account consumer's rights effectively to provide the minimum
level of liability for the programmer

- for developers, the notions of "covered work" and “aggregate” are
different than the mechanism of “external modules” and “internal modules”
more flexible.  With CeCILL, the programmer can choose to develop an
internal module if he wants to distribute its development under CeCILL but
he still has the choice to develop an external module if he prefers to
choose another license for this module.



To elaborate more on the better legal safety:

- The mention of a (reasonable) applicable law considerably reduces the
risk of having a judge declare some provisions of the license invalid or
interpret some provisions differently from the intent of the authors of the
license. The Munich court that examined in 2004 the GPL determined that
German law should apply but nevertheless was not able to tell whether some
clauses of the GPL are really valid or not (according to the German
Copyright Act). That examplifies legal risks of the GPL, at least in Europe.

Even if CeCILL is submitted to the French Law, it  was written to be
conformant to the relevant European directives and regulations (directive
on the legal protection of computer programs, directive on unfair terms in
consumer contracts, directive on the approximation of the laws, regulations
and administrative provisions of the Member States concerning liability for
defective products, convention on the law applicable to contractual
obligations, and regulation on jurisdiction and the recognition and
enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters). That makes it as
close as possible to what a multinational (European) license can be now.



2. The license must be clearly written, simple, and understandable.



Although CeCILL has been written and reviewed by lawyers, it has been
designed to be read and understood by a programmer (computer scientists and
software engineers were indeed part of the team that wrote the license).
Note that although the text of CeCILL is significantly longer than the text
of other Open Source licenses, we believe that it makes CeCILL much clearer
than most shorter licenses.



We now have more than 6 years experience with the version 2 of CeCILL that
has been debated by various non legal Open Source Software users and we
collected a lot of feedback from programmers.

As recommended by OSI board in 2005, we choose to modify articles 5.3.1
and 5.3.2 of CeCILL v.2.1 in order to clarify the obligation of the

source code of the software,

distribution of the modified software.





3. The license must be reusable.



CeCILL is clearly reusable (it has not been designed for a specific
Program or specific licensees or licensors)

-       The Affero GPL license v.3

-       The EUPL v.1.1.

distribution of software, including modified software, under the same or
similar open source license. These similarities are on the principles: from
a legal point of view, CeCILL license v.2.1 is really different.


*Why this license was not sufficient for our needs: *



At first, these licenses don’t clearly refer to an applicable law. We
believe that it’s as necessary for open source licenses to refer to an
applicable law as for others type of agreements because it reduces legal
uncertainties for companies: in case of litigation, the dispute can be
easily analyzed by lawyers and companies don’t have to wait for the judge
decision to know which the applicable law is.



Moreover, theses licenses are not, in our opinion, sufficiently clear on
developments which shall be keep under the same license:

-       In GPL v.3 and Affero GPL v.3 the difference between the covered
works and an aggregate is not simple to understand in all cases *(“**A
compilation of a covered work with other separate and independent works,
which are not by their nature extensions of the covered work, and which are
not combined with it such as to form a larger program, in or on a volume of
a storage or distribution medium, is called an “aggregate” if the
compilation and its resulting copyright are not used to limit the access or
legal rights of the compilation's users beyond what the individual works
permit. Inclusion of a covered work in an aggregate does not cause this

works or software that could be created by the Licensee, based upon the

extent of modification or dependence on the Original Work required in order
to classify a work as a Derivative Work; this extent is determined by
copyright law applicable in the country mentioned in Article 15”*. This
definition undertakes users to search themselves for each software program
distributed under EUPL v.1.1 which is the applicable law and, in this law,
which is the meaning of a derivative work.



Furthermore in terms of compatibility, the EUPL doesn’t include the GNU
GPL v3 on its compatibility clause list having these two licenses
“copyleft” provisions in conflict.



However, CeCILL includes a provision that allows the distribution of its
code within code covered by GNU GPL, making it explicitly compatible with
any version of the GNU GPL including the v3.



We also believe that CeciLL covers many details of software law, such as
the right to translate,  provides efficient and detailed provisions about
using rights, distribution rights, warranties and responsibility.



CeciLL also provides a satisfying solution to issues on moral rights of
the authors and compatibility with other licenses.



According to these developments, we believe that CeCILL is safer from a
legal point of view.

conjunction with software distributed under other open source licenses:*

other open source licenses. This license contains no restrictions as to
possible use together with other software.

covered by CeCILL is combined with a work covered by Affero GPL, the Affero
GPL takes precedence (see clause 5.3.4 of CeCILL).

Any software licenses that are entirely incompatible with the GNU GPL.

Concerning the three criteria here is our analysis:



*1. The license must not be duplicative*

* *

CeCILL v.2.1 retains the principles of the GNU GPL but it cannot be seen
as duplicative for the following reasons. We believe that CeCILL is worth
adding as an Open Source license because it addresses the corresponding
problems not addressed by the GPL: better and safer legal foundation (at
least in Europe), better protection of the programmer and clearer
mechanisms:

CeCILL is very different. Moreover, the liability clause of CeCILL is
taking into account consumer's rights effectively to provide the minimum
level of liability for the programmer

different than the mechanism of “external modules” and “internal modules”
more flexible.  With CeCILL, the programmer can choose to develop an
internal module if he wants to distribute its development under CeCILL but

risk of having a judge declare some provisions of the license invalid or

enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters). That makes it as

designed to be read and understood by a programmer (computer scientists and
software engineers were indeed part of the team that wrote the license).

of other Open Source licenses, we believe that it makes CeCILL much clearer
than most shorter licenses.

has been debated by various non legal Open Source Software users and we
collected a lot of feedback from programmers.

- _Part one: The existing OSI-approved license that is most similar to
CeCILL: _
Since 2005, the GNU GPL stays the most similar OSI approved license to
CeCILL. The publication of the GPL license v.3 doesn't change the
similarity between the 2 licenses.
Nevertheless, since 2005, we have noted 2 others licenses similar to
CeCILL:
-The Affero GPL license v.3
-The EUPL v.1.1.
As CeCILL license, all these licenses have the same aim of maintaining
the distribution of software, including modified software, under the
same or similar open source license. These similarities are on the
principles: from a legal point of view, CeCILL license v.2.1 is really
different.
_Why this license was not sufficient for our needs:_
At first, these licenses don't clearly refer to an applicable law. We
believe that it's as necessary for open source licenses to refer to an
applicable law as for others type of agreements because it reduces
legal uncertainties for companies: in case of litigation, the dispute
can be easily analyzed by lawyers and companies don't have to wait for
the judge decision to know which the applicable law is.
Moreover, theses licenses are not, in our opinion, sufficiently clear
on developments which shall be keep under the same license:
-In GPL v.3 and Affero GPL v.3 the difference between the covered
works and an aggregate is not simple to understand in all cases /("//A
compilation of a covered work with other separate and independent
works, which are not by their nature extensions of the covered work,
and which are not combined with it such as to form a larger program,
in or on a volume of a storage or distribution medium, is called an
"aggregate" if the compilation and its resulting copyright are not
used to limit the access or legal rights of the compilation's users
beyond what the individual works permit. Inclusion of a covered work
in an aggregate does not cause this License to apply to the other
parts of the aggregate.")/;
-the "derivatives works" in the EUPL v.1.1 are defined as /"the works
or software that could be created by the Licensee, based upon the
Original Work or modifications thereof. This Licence does not define
the extent of modification or dependence on the Original Work required
in order to classify a work as a Derivative Work; this extent is
determined by copyright law applicable in the country mentioned in
Article 15"/. This definition undertakes users to search themselves
for each software program distributed under EUPL v.1.1 which is the
applicable law and, in this law, which is the meaning of a derivative
work.
Furthermore in terms of compatibility, the EUPL doesn't include the
GNU GPL v3 on its compatibility clause list having these two licenses
"copyleft" provisions in conflict.
However, CeCILL includes a provision that allows the distribution of
its code within code covered by GNU GPL, making it explicitly
compatible with any version of the GNU GPL including the v3.
We also believe that CeciLL covers many details of software law, such
as the right to translate,provides efficient and detailed provisions
about using rights, distribution rights, warranties and responsibility.
CeciLL also provides a satisfying solution to issues on moral rights
of the authors and compatibility with other licenses.
According to these developments, we believe that CeCILL is safer from
a legal point of view.
- _Part two: How software distributed under your license can be used
in conjunction with software distributed under other open source
licenses:_
Software distributed under CeCILL license v.2.1 can be used freely
with other open source licenses. This license contains no restrictions
as to possibleuse together with other software.
CeCILL provides, since its version 2.0, a special exception for the
GPL license. In its version 2.1, we add another special exception:
when a work covered by CeCILL is combined with a work covered by
Affero GPL, the Affero GPL takes precedence (see clause 5.3.4 of CeCILL).
_Software licenses that are entirely incompatible with CeCILL:_
Any software licenses that are entirely incompatible with the GNU GPL.
_- Part three: _the plain text of CeCILL v.2.1 follows.
Concerning the three criteria here is our analysis:
_1. The license must not be duplicative_
CeCILL v.2.1 retains the principles of the GNU GPL but it cannot be
seen as duplicative for the following reasons. We believe that CeCILL
is worth adding as an Open Source license because it addresses the
corresponding problems not addressed by the GPL: better and safer
legal foundation (at least in Europe), better protection of the
programmer and clearer mechanisms:
- from a legal point of view, at least by referring to a specific law,
CeCILL is very different. Moreover, the liability clause of CeCILL is
taking into account consumer's rights effectively to provide the
minimum level of liability for the programmer
- for developers, the notions of "covered work" and "aggregate" are
different than the mechanism of"external modules" and "internal
modules" more flexible. With CeCILL, the programmer can choose to
develop an internal module if he wants to distribute its development
under CeCILL but he still has the choice to develop an external module
if he prefers to choose another license for this module.
To elaborate more on the better legal safety:
- The mention of a (reasonable) applicable law considerably reduces
the risk of having a judge declare some provisions of the license
invalid or interpret some provisions differently from the intent of
the authors of the license. The Munich court that examined in 2004 the
GPL determined that German law should apply but nevertheless was not
able to tell whether some clauses of the GPL are really valid or not
(according to the German Copyright Act). That examplifies legal risks
of the GPL, at least in Europe.
Even if CeCILL is submitted to the French Law, it was written to be
conformant to the relevant European directives and regulations
(directive on the legal protection of computer programs, directive on
unfair terms in consumer contracts, directive on the approximation of
the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the Member
States concerning liability for defective products, convention on the
law applicable to contractual obligations, and regulation on
jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil
and commercial matters). That makes it as close as possible to what a
multinational (European) license can be now.
2. The license must be clearly written, simple, and understandable.
Although CeCILL has been written and reviewed by lawyers, it has been
designed to be read and understood by a programmer (computer
scientists and software engineers were indeed part of the team that
wrote the license). Note that although the text of CeCILL is
significantly longer than the text of other Open Source licenses, we
believe that it makes CeCILL much clearer than most shorter licenses.
We now have more than 6 years experience with the version 2 of CeCILL
that has been debated by various non legal Open Source Software users
and we collected a lot of feedback from programmers.
As recommended by OSI board in 2005, we choose to modify articles
5.3.1 and 5.3.2 of CeCILL v.2.1 in order to clarify the obligation of
the licensee to allow access to the source code in the event that only

provides that:

code of the software,
-this obligation is limited in time : at least 3 years from the
distribution of the modified software.
3. The license must be reusable.
CeCILL is clearly reusable (it has not been designed for a specific
Program or specific licensees or licensors)

timeline.subject: [License-review] CeCILL license V2.1 for Approval
timeline.snippet: Submits CeCILL v2.1 for OSI approval, explaining it addresses the source-distribution clarity issues that caused v2.0's 2005 rejection and is backed by CEA, CNRS and Inria.
timeline.point_zh: 提交 CeCILL v2.1 供 OSI 审批，说明该版本解决了导致 v2.0 于 2005 年被拒的源代码分发措辞不清问题，并由 CEA、CNRS 和 Inria 支持。
timeline.point: Submits CeCILL v2.1 for OSI approval, explaining it addresses the source-distribution clarity issues that caused v2.0's 2005 rejection and is backed by CEA, CNRS and Inria.

timeline.subject: [License-review] CeCILL license V2.1 for Approval
timeline.snippet: Expresses hope that CeCILL will be approved by OSI, noting that significant free software such as SciLAB uses it and that it is essentially the French variant of the GPL.
timeline.point_zh: 表示希望 CeCILL 能获得 OSI 批准，指出 SciLAB 等重要自由软件使用该许可证，且其本质上是 GPL 的法国版本。
timeline.point: Expresses hope that CeCILL will be approved by OSI, noting that significant free software such as SciLAB uses it and that it is essentially the French variant of the GPL.

timeline.subject: [License-review] CeCILL license V2.1 for Approval

timeline.point: Thanks John Cowan for the explanation of how bilingual authentic-text clauses are interpreted by courts.

timeline.subject: [License-review] CeCILL license V2.1 for Approval
timeline.snippet: Argues the bilingual language question is less important than substantive concerns about other CeCILL articles (6.4, 6.2, 7, and 11.1) for the review's purposes.
timeline.point_zh: 认为双语条款问题不如对 CeCILL 其他条款（6.4、6.2、7 和 11.1）的实质性关注重要。

timeline.snippet: Criticizes CeCILL's use of the vague term "intellectual property rights" in sections 6.4 and 6.2, arguing the license should instead name the specific rights (i.e. copyright) it actually addresses.
timeline.point_zh: 批评 CeCILL 在 6.4 和 6.2 条中使用模糊的“知识产权”一词，主张应明确指出实际涉及的权利（即著作权）。

timeline.subject: For (Legacy?) Approval: The MirOS Licence
timeline.snippet: Re-submits the MirOS Licence for OSI approval, describing it as a compact, BSD-spirit licence optimized for European citizens and EU law, with full permissions wording and DFSG/OSD compliance.
timeline.point_zh: 重新提交 MirOS 许可证申请 OSI 审批，将其描述为一款紧凑的、继承 BSD 精神、针对欧洲公民和欧盟法律优化的许可证，措辞完整且符合 DFSG/OSD。
timeline.point: Re-submits the MirOS Licence for OSI approval, describing it as a compact, BSD-spirit licence optimized for European citizens and EU law, with full permissions wording and DFSG/OSD compliance.

timeline.subject: For (Legacy?) Approval: The MirOS Licence
timeline.snippet: Defends re-submitting the MirOS Licence, arguing it should be approved because it conforms to the OSD, is in active use, and is needed because some hosting platforms discriminate against non-OSI-approved licences.
timeline.point_zh: 为重新提交 MirOS 许可证辩护，认为应获批准，因其符合 OSD、正在积极使用，且部分托管平台歧视非 OSI 批准的许可证。
timeline.point: Defends re-submitting the MirOS Licence, arguing it should be approved because it conforms to the OSD, is in active use, and is needed because some hosting platforms discriminate against non-OSI-approved licences.

timeline.subject: For (Legacy?) Approval: The MirOS Licence
timeline.snippet: Questions why the ISC licence (which lacks OKD conformance and has questionable language) was approved while the MirOS Licence is being resisted, and clarifies that advertising clauses were already removed.
timeline.point_zh: 质疑为何缺乏 OKD 一致性且措辞存疑的 ISC 许可证已获批准，而 MirOS 许可证却受阻，并澄清广告条款已被移除。
timeline.point: Questions why the ISC licence (which lacks OKD conformance and has questionable language) was approved while the MirOS Licence is being resisted, and clarifies that advertising clauses were already removed.

timeline.subject: For (Legacy?) Approval: The MirOS Licence
timeline.snippet: Sarcastically suggests that if the ISC licence shouldn't have been approved either, then perhaps its approval should be withdrawn.
timeline.point_zh: 讽刺地表示如果 ISC 许可证也不应获批，那么或许应撤销其批准。
timeline.point: Sarcastically suggests that if the ISC licence shouldn't have been approved either, then perhaps its approval should be withdrawn.

timeline.subject: For (Legacy?) Approval: The MirOS Licence
timeline.snippet: Counters that the FSF does not limit itself to recommending only GPL-family licences when assessing freedom, and notes that licence proliferation is mainly a problem for reciprocal licences, not permissive ones.
timeline.point_zh: 反驳 FSF 在评定自由度时并不局限于 GPL 系列许可证，并指出许可证泛滥主要是互惠性许可证的问题，而非宽松许可证。
timeline.point: Counters that the FSF does not limit itself to recommending only GPL-family licences when assessing freedom, and notes that licence proliferation is mainly a problem for reciprocal licences, not permissive ones.

timeline.subject: For (Legacy?) Approval: The MirOS Licence
timeline.snippet: Acknowledges permissive is better for proliferation concerns but questions whether a permissive license can truly be treated as equivalent to public domain, referencing the Jacobsen case.
timeline.point_zh: 承认宽松许可证在泛滥问题上较好，但质疑宽松许可证是否真能等同于公有领域，提及 Jacobsen 案。
timeline.point: Acknowledges permissive is better for proliferation concerns but questions whether a permissive license can truly be treated as equivalent to public domain, referencing the Jacobsen case.

aliases: Request for approval: EUPL (European Union Public Licence)

osi_api.name: The European Union Public License, version 1.1

board_vote.motion_text: Approve the European Union Public License (EUPL) v1.2

timeline.subject: Request for approval: EUPL (European Union Public Licence)
timeline.snippet: Contains no substantive archived body in the EUPL approval request thread.
timeline.point_zh: 在 EUPL 批准请求线程中没有可提取的实质归档正文。
timeline.point: Contains no substantive archived body in the EUPL approval request thread.

timeline.subject: Request for approval: EUPL (European Union Public Licence)
timeline.snippet: Dismisses the hypothetical of free software in a totalitarian state as unrealistic, and notes the counterparty is merely repeating prior arguments without adding new information.
timeline.point_zh: 认为在极权国家讨论自由软件的假设不切实际，并指出对方只是在重复既有论点而未提供新信息。
timeline.point: Dismisses the hypothetical of free software in a totalitarian state as unrealistic, and notes the counterparty is merely repeating prior arguments without adding new information.

timeline.subject: Request for approval: EUPL (European Union Public Licence)
timeline.snippet: Argues that OSI should distinguish choice of law from jurisdiction venue, and that a license-as-contract may legitimately specify EU law even for non-EU parties, analogous to AAA arbitration clauses.
timeline.point_zh: 主张 OSI 应区分法律选择与管辖法院，认为作为合同的许可证即使对非欧盟当事方约定适用欧盟法也合理，类似于约定 AAA 仲裁。
timeline.point: Argues that OSI should distinguish choice of law from jurisdiction venue, and that a license-as-contract may legitimately specify EU law even for non-EU parties, analogous to AAA arbitration clauses.

timeline.subject: Request for approval: EUPL (European Union Public Licence)
timeline.snippet: Questions whether EUPL Article 11's requirement to disclose licensor name and address is intrusive (possibly aiding patent trolls) and asks whether EU law already mandates it, making the license clause redundant.
timeline.point_zh: 质疑 EUPL 第 11 条要求披露许可人姓名与地址是否具有侵入性（或有利于专利流氓），并询问欧盟法是否已作要求、是否无需在许可证中重复。
timeline.point: Questions whether EUPL Article 11's requirement to disclose licensor name and address is intrusive (possibly aiding patent trolls) and asks whether EU law already mandates it, making the license clause redundant.

timeline.subject: Request for approval: EUPL (European Union Public Licence)
timeline.snippet: Agrees OSI should not reject non-English licenses by default, but questions whether the review lists can realistically evaluate licenses in languages other than English (with limited French/German/Spanish capacity).
timeline.point_zh: 同意 OSI 不应默认拒绝非英语许可证，但质疑审阅列表是否具备评审英语以外语言许可证的现实能力（法语、德语、西班牙语或勉强可行）。
timeline.point: Agrees OSI should not reject non-English licenses by default, but questions whether the review lists can realistically evaluate licenses in languages other than English (with limited French/German/Spanish capacity).

timeline.subject: Request for approval: EUPL (European Union Public Licence)
timeline.snippet: Submits the draft EUPL v1.1 for OSI review in place of v1.0, explaining that reviewer feedback and a 50-expert EC workshop produced seven clarifying modifications, and invites comment.
timeline.point_zh: 提交 EUPL v1.1 草案以替代 v1.0 供 OSI 审阅，说明审阅者反馈与 EC 50 人专家研讨会促成了七项澄清性修改，并邀请评论。
timeline.point: Submits the draft EUPL v1.1 for OSI review in place of v1.0, explaining that reviewer feedback and a 50-expert EC workshop produced seven clarifying modifications, and invites comment.

timeline.subject: Request for approval: EUPL (European Union Public Licence)
timeline.snippet: Supports approval of EUPL 1.1 while expressing disappointment that GPLv3/AGPLv3 were not added to the compatibility list, and flagging that the new Distribution definition makes the license Affero-style (still OSD-compliant).
timeline.point_zh: 支持批准 EUPL 1.1，但对未将 GPLv3/AGPLv3 纳入兼容清单表示失望，并指出新的分发定义使许可证呈现 Affero 式特征（仍符合 OSD）。
timeline.point: Supports approval of EUPL 1.1 while expressing disappointment that GPLv3/AGPLv3 were not added to the compatibility list, and flagging that the new Distribution definition makes the license Affero-style (still OSD-compliant).

board_vote.motion_text: Approve the European Union Public License (EUPL) v1.2

timeline.subject: request for Legacy Approval of the NTP License

submissions.name: GNU Affero General Public License version 3
aliases: For approval: GNU Affero General Public License

osi_api.name: GNU Affero General Public License version 3

timeline.subject: For approval: GNU Affero General Public License
timeline.snippet: Submits the GNU Affero GPLv3 (AGPLv3) to OSI for approval, explaining it closes the ASP loophole by requiring source availability for remote network interaction. Argues it is consistent with the OSD.
timeline.point_zh: 向 OSI 提交 GNU Affero GPLv3 (AGPLv3) 请求批准，解释其通过要求远程网络交互的源码可用性来堵住 ASP 漏洞。主张其与 OSD 一致。
timeline.point: Submits the GNU Affero GPLv3 (AGPLv3) to OSI for approval, explaining it closes the ASP loophole by requiring source availability for remote network interaction. Argues it is consistent with the OSD.

timeline.subject: For approval: GNU Affero General Public License
timeline.snippet: Supports AGPLv3 approval but questions the proliferation category, arguing it should be classified as a special-purpose license rather than widely used.
timeline.point_zh: 支持批准 AGPLv3，但质疑其分类，认为应归为特殊用途许可证而非广泛使用的许可证。
timeline.point: Supports AGPLv3 approval but questions the proliferation category, arguing it should be classified as a special-purpose license rather than widely used.

timeline.subject: For approval: GNU Affero General Public License
timeline.snippet: Agrees AGPLv3 appears OSD-compliant and concurs it should be classified as a special-purpose license.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 AGPLv3 看起来符合 OSD，同意将其归类为特殊用途许可证。
timeline.point: Agrees AGPLv3 appears OSD-compliant and concurs it should be classified as a special-purpose license.

timeline.subject: For approval: GNU Affero General Public License
timeline.snippet: Disagrees that AGPLv3 is special-purpose, arguing it doesn't serve a specific organizational need any more than GPLv3 or Apache 2. Compares closing the ASP loophole to Apache 2 closing the software patents loophole.
timeline.point_zh: 不同意 AGPLv3 是特殊用途许可证，认为它与 GPLv3 或 Apache 2 一样不服务于特定组织需求。将堵住 ASP 漏洞类比为 Apache 2 堵住软件专利漏洞。
timeline.point: Disagrees that AGPLv3 is special-purpose, arguing it doesn't serve a specific organizational need any more than GPLv3 or Apache 2. Compares closing the ASP loophole to Apache 2 closing the software patents loophole.

timeline.subject: For approval: GNU Affero General Public License
timeline.snippet: Suggests AGPLv3 should be classified as 'Other/Miscellaneous licenses' similar to the Open Software License.
timeline.point_zh: 建议 AGPLv3 应与 Open Software License 一样归类为「其他/杂项许可证」。
timeline.point: Suggests AGPLv3 should be classified as 'Other/Miscellaneous licenses' similar to the Open Software License.

timeline.subject: For approval: GNU Affero General Public License
timeline.snippet: Argues AGPLv3 may not be enforceable under US copyright law, citing 17 USC 117(a)(1) and case law (Aymes v. Bonelli, Krause v. Titleserv) that grants owners the right to modify software for business needs, including over a network.
timeline.point_zh: 质疑 AGPLv3 在美国版权法下的可执行性，引用 17 USC 117(a)(1) 和判例法（Aymes v. Bonelli、Krause v. Titleserv），认为软件所有者有权为业务需求（包括通过网络）修改软件。
timeline.point: Argues AGPLv3 may not be enforceable under US copyright law, citing 17 USC 117(a)(1) and case law (Aymes v. Bonelli, Krause v. Titleserv) that grants owners the right to modify software for business needs, including over a network.

timeline.subject: For approval: GNU Affero General Public License
timeline.snippet: Notes that their organization (ossdiscovery.org) also uses AGPL and did not consider it a special-purpose license when choosing it.
timeline.point_zh: 指出其组织 (ossdiscovery.org) 也使用 AGPL，选择时并未将其视为特殊用途许可证。
timeline.point: Notes that their organization (ossdiscovery.org) also uses AGPL and did not consider it a special-purpose license when choosing it.

timeline.subject: For approval: GNU Affero General Public License
timeline.snippet: Argues that if AGPLv3 were truly general-purpose, it would simply be the GPLv3, implying its network interaction requirement makes it inherently specialized.
timeline.point_zh: 认为如果 AGPLv3 真的是通用许可证，它就应该是 GPLv3，暗示其网络交互要求使其本质上是专门化的。
timeline.point: Argues that if AGPLv3 were truly general-purpose, it would simply be the GPLv3, implying its network interaction requirement makes it inherently specialized.

timeline.subject: For approval: GNU Affero General Public License
timeline.snippet: Seeks agreement on what 'special purpose' means in OSI License Proliferation categories, arguing AGPLv3 addresses the ASP loophole just as Apache 2 addresses software patents and GPLv3 addresses internationalization.
timeline.point_zh: 希望就 OSI 许可证激增分类中「特殊用途」的定义达成一致，认为 AGPLv3 解决 ASP 漏洞正如 Apache 2 解决软件专利漏洞、GPLv3 解决国际化问题。
timeline.point: Seeks agreement on what 'special purpose' means in OSI License Proliferation categories, arguing AGPLv3 addresses the ASP loophole just as Apache 2 addresses software patents and GPLv3 addresses internationalization.

timeline.subject: Æsthetic Permissive License - For Approval
timeline.snippet: Submits a new minimal permissive license (under five lines) for OSI review, arguing no existing license is both permissive with a warranty disclaimer, applicable to a single work, and under the McQuary line limit.

submissions.name: Frameworx License 1.0
aliases: Frameworx license clause 3b

timeline.subject: Frameworx license clause 3b
timeline.snippet: Questions whether Frameworx clause 3b (requiring Value-Added Services pricing to be commensurate with fair market value and supportive of the license's intent) is consistent with the OSD, calling it a restraint on commercial activity.
timeline.point_zh: 质疑 Frameworx 第 3b 条（要求增值服务定价与公允市值相称并支持许可协议意图）是否符合 OSD，认为这构成对商业活动的限制。
timeline.point: Questions whether Frameworx clause 3b (requiring Value-Added Services pricing to be commensurate with fair market value and supportive of the license's intent) is consistent with the OSD, calling it a restraint on commercial activity.

timeline.subject: Frameworx license clause 3b
timeline.snippet: Argues the clause is harmless for commercial services but could wrongly bar non-commercial derivative deployment.
timeline.point_zh: 主张该条款对商业服务可能只是同义反复，但会不当地禁止非商业衍生部署。
timeline.point: Argues the clause is harmless for commercial services but could wrongly bar non-commercial derivative deployment.

timeline.subject: Frameworx license clause 3b
timeline.snippet: Agrees the clause may be fine for overcharging but problematic in practice, and reads it as excluding academic-style commercial-use licenses.
timeline.point_zh: 同意该条款对超额收费也许无碍，但现实中可能出问题，并认为它意在排除需要商业用途额外许可的学术式许可证。
timeline.point: Agrees the clause may be fine for overcharging but problematic in practice, and reads it as excluding academic-style commercial-use licenses.

timeline.subject: Frameworx license clause 3b
timeline.snippet: Interprets the clause as applying only to commercial or fee-based services, not non-commercial ones.
timeline.point_zh: 将该条款解释为只适用于商业或收费服务，不约束非商业服务。
timeline.point: Interprets the clause as applying only to commercial or fee-based services, not non-commercial ones.

timeline.subject: Frameworx license clause 3b
timeline.snippet: Argues the clause was meant to prevent hidden markups, but says that reading would still violate the OSD.
timeline.point_zh: 认为该条款本意是防止隐性加价，但这种解读仍会违反 OSD。
timeline.point: Argues the clause was meant to prevent hidden markups, but says that reading would still violate the OSD.

timeline.subject: Frameworx license clause 3b
timeline.snippet: Says the clause targets hosting and commercial pricing, and treats it as an OSD #6 violation.
timeline.point_zh: 认为该条款针对托管和商业定价，构成 OSD #6 违反。
timeline.point: Says the clause targets hosting and commercial pricing, and treats it as an OSD #6 violation.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Microsoft Public License
timeline.snippet: Formally submits the Microsoft Public License (renamed from MS-Permissive) for OSI approval, arguing it offers simplicity, brevity, and permissive terms with IP protection.
timeline.point_zh: 正式提交 Microsoft 公共许可证（由 MS-Permissive 更名）申请 OSI 批准，认为该许可证兼具简洁性、宽松性与知识产权保护。
timeline.point: Formally submits the Microsoft Public License (renamed from MS-Permissive) for OSI approval, arguing it offers simplicity, brevity, and permissive terms with IP protection.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Microsoft Public License
timeline.snippet: Asks for clarification on what "the same requirements" means for the object-form license, specifically whether it must include a copyright grant like clause 2(A).
timeline.point_zh: 追问“相同要求”对目标代码形式许可证的确切含义，特别是否需要包含类似第 2(A) 条的版权授权。
timeline.point: Asks for clarification on what "the same requirements" means for the object-form license, specifically whether it must include a copyright grant like clause 2(A).

timeline.subject: For Approval: Microsoft Public License
timeline.snippet: Argues that while MS-PL/MS-CL may letter-of-the-law comply with OSD, Microsoft conflation of Open Source and Shared Source terms and the interplay of SDK licenses undermine the spirit of the Open Source definition.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 MS-PL/MS-CL 虽然在字面上可能符合 OSD，但微软将“开源”和“共享源“混为一谈，加上 SDK 许可证的限制，违背了开源定义的精神。
timeline.point: Argues that while MS-PL/MS-CL may letter-of-the-law comply with OSD, Microsoft conflation of Open Source and Shared Source terms and the interplay of SDK licenses undermine the spirit of the Open Source definition.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Microsoft Public License
timeline.snippet: Counters that OSI does not own the Open Source trademark and questions whether Microsoft actually abuses the term, suggesting an enforceable OSI-compliant logo would better address the issue.
timeline.point_zh: 反驳称 OSI 并不拥有“开源”商标，质疑微软是否真的滥用了该术语，建议采用可强制执行的 OSI 合规标志来解决该问题。
timeline.point: Counters that OSI does not own the Open Source trademark and questions whether Microsoft actually abuses the term, suggesting an enforceable OSI-compliant logo would better address the issue.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Microsoft Public License
timeline.snippet: Argues against a double standard: if open source means OSI-approved, then many existing projects (OpenSSL, PostgreSQL) would also need to submit their licenses, leading to license proliferation.
timeline.point_zh: 反对双重标准：如果“开源”等同于 OSI 批准，则 OpenSSL、PostgreSQL 等项目的许可证也需要提交，导致许可证泊滥。
timeline.point: Argues against a double standard: if open source means OSI-approved, then many existing projects (OpenSSL, PostgreSQL) would also need to submit their licenses, leading to license proliferation.

timeline.point: Archived content is only a scrubbed HTML attachment, with no extractable Microsoft Public License argument.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Non-Profit OSL 3.0
timeline.snippet: Submits the Non-Profit OSL 3.0 for OSI approval on behalf of IETF. The license is a variant of OSL 3.0 tailored for non-profit organizations, removing the warranty of provenance and limiting liability for direct damages, while maintaining the same reciprocal open source requirements.
timeline.point_zh: 代表 IETF 提交 Non-Profit OSL 3.0 供 OSI 审批。该许可证是 OSL 3.0 的非营利组织变体，取消了来源保证并限制直接损害赔偿责任，同时保持相同的互惠开源要求。
timeline.point: Submits the Non-Profit OSL 3.0 for OSI approval on behalf of IETF. The license is a variant of OSL 3.0 tailored for non-profit organizations, removing the warranty of provenance and limiting liability for direct damages, while maintaining the same reciprocal open source requirements.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Non-Profit OSL 3.0
timeline.snippet: Supports approval of the Non-Profit OSL 3.0 but suggests fixing section 16 to properly reference the NOSL name.
timeline.point_zh: 支持批准 Non-Profit OSL 3.0，但建议修正第 16 条以正确引用 NOSL 名称。
timeline.point: Supports approval of the Non-Profit OSL 3.0 but suggests fixing section 16 to properly reference the NOSL name.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Non-Profit OSL 3.0
timeline.snippet: Seconds the approval but raises a concern that section 17(d)'s requirement for non-profit organizations to relicense under OSL may encroach on OSD #7 and #5. Questions what IETF gains from this requirement.
timeline.point_zh: 附议批准但提出担忧，第 17(d) 条要求非营利组织在 OSL 下重新许可可能侵犯 OSD 第 7 条和第 5 条。质疑 IETF 从该要求中获得什么价值。
timeline.point: Seconds the approval but raises a concern that section 17(d)'s requirement for non-profit organizations to relicense under OSL may encroach on OSD #7 and #5. Questions what IETF gains from this requirement.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Non-Profit OSL 3.0
timeline.snippet: Explains that section 17(d)'s requirement exists because commercial suppliers should offer warranty of provenance and accept liability, which benefits open source customers. Notes IETF did not request this requirement and that the license remains OSD-compliant.
timeline.point_zh: 解释第 17(d) 条要求存在的原因是商业供应商应提供来源保证并承担直接损害赔偿责任，这有利于开源用户。指出 IETF 未要求此条款，许可证仍符合 OSD。
timeline.point: Explains that section 17(d)'s requirement exists because commercial suppliers should offer warranty of provenance and accept liability, which benefits open source customers. Notes IETF did not request this requirement and that the license remains OSD-compliant.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Non-Profit OSL 3.0
timeline.snippet: Argues that the warranty requirement discriminates against a field of endeavour and should be replaced with explanatory text about the benefits of offering warranties.

board_vote.motion_text: GPLv3 & LGPLv3 — we approve these licenses with the following statement: “The Open Source Initiative is pleased to announce that, based on broad review and acceptance by both the Board and the community, it has confirmed that GPLv3 and LGPLv3 both conform to the Open Source Definition. Note that new licenses containing “further restrictions” allowed by GPLv3 and LGPLv3 may not be conformant with the OSD, and thus will still require separate review and approval. Due to the dramatic differences between and viable communities around both the GPLv3 family and the GPLv2 family of licenses, we will not be marking GPLv2 and LGPLv2 as redundant, even thought they are technically superseded respectively by GPLv3 and LGPLv3.”

board_vote.motion_text: GPLv3 & LGPLv3 — we approve these licenses with the following statement: “The Open Source Initiative is pleased to announce that, based on broad review and acceptance by both the Board and the community, it has confirmed that GPLv3 and LGPLv3 both conform to the Open Source Definition. Note that new licenses containing “further restrictions” allowed by GPLv3 and LGPLv3 may not be conformant with the OSD, and thus will still require separate review and approval. Due to the dramatic differences between and viable communities around both the GPLv3 family and the GPLv2 family of licenses, we will not be marking GPLv2 and LGPLv2 as redundant, even thought they are technically superseded respectively by GPLv3 and LGPLv3.”

board_vote.motion_text: GPLv3 & LGPLv3 — we approve these licenses with the following statement: “The Open Source Initiative is pleased to announce that, based on broad review and acceptance by both the Board and the community, it has confirmed that GPLv3 and LGPLv3 both conform to the Open Source Definition. Note that new licenses containing “further restrictions” allowed by GPLv3 and LGPLv3 may not be conformant with the OSD, and thus will still require separate review and approval. Due to the dramatic differences between and viable communities around both the GPLv3 family and the GPLv2 family of licenses, we will not be marking GPLv2 and LGPLv2 as redundant, even thought they are technically superseded respectively by GPLv3 and LGPLv3.”

timeline.subject: For Approval: Common Public Attribution License (CPAL)
timeline.snippet: Submits the CPAL for OSI approval, explaining it builds on the MPL with attribution (Section 14) and network-use (Section 15) provisions drawn from existing approved licenses, and that it ceased calling itself open source pending approval.
timeline.point_zh: 提交 CPAL 供 OSI 审批，说明其基于 MPL，新增的署名条款（第 14 条）和网络使用条款（第 15 条）借鉴自已批准的许可证，并表示在获批前不再自称开源。
timeline.point: Submits the CPAL for OSI approval, explaining it builds on the MPL with attribution (Section 14) and network-use (Section 15) provisions drawn from existing approved licenses, and that it ceased calling itself open source pending approval.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Common Public Attribution License (CPAL)
timeline.snippet: Thanks Socialtext for ceasing to call itself open source pre-approval, but argues CPAL's required display of an arbitrary logo on GUIs violates OSD #10, that the subjective "prominent" definition creates an OSD #3 problem, and that the application-needs-attribution rationale is unfounded.
timeline.point_zh: 感谢 Socialtext 在获批前不再自称开源，但主张 CPAL 强制 GUI 显示任意 logo 违反 OSD #10，主观的“显著”定义会造成 OSD #3 问题，并以应用需要署名为由的论据站不住脚。
timeline.point: Thanks Socialtext for ceasing to call itself open source pre-approval, but argues CPAL's required display of an arbitrary logo on GUIs violates OSD #10, that the subjective "prominent" definition creates an OSD #3 problem, and that the application-needs-attribution rationale is unfounded.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Common Public Attribution License (CPAL)
timeline.snippet: Concedes his earlier point was implied rather than stated, and clarifies that any "sufficient duration" interpretation could eventually make merging multiple CPAL programs impractical due to attribution accumulation, creating a disincentive to merge.
timeline.point_zh: 承认此前观点为暗示而非明言，并澄清任何“足够持续时间”的解释都可能因署名累积而最终使合并多个 CPAL 程序变得不切实际，从而抑制合并。
timeline.point: Concedes his earlier point was implied rather than stated, and clarifies that any "sufficient duration" interpretation could eventually make merging multiple CPAL programs impractical due to attribution accumulation, creating a disincentive to merge.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Common Public Attribution License (CPAL)
timeline.snippet: Argues CPAL's redefinition of "commercial use" is confusing and could subvert the OSD, that it arguably discriminates against non-commercial use, and that licensing "Use" itself implies a use-without-licence restriction; discourages such questionable wording in derived licences.
timeline.point_zh: 主张 CPAL 对“商业使用”的重新定义令人困惑且可能规避 OSD，可能歧视非商业使用，且将“使用”纳入许可范围暗示无许可证即不可使用；不鼓励衍生许可证采用此类可疑措辞。
timeline.point: Argues CPAL's redefinition of "commercial use" is confusing and could subvert the OSD, that it arguably discriminates against non-commercial use, and that licensing "Use" itself implies a use-without-licence restriction; discourages such questionable wording in derived licences.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Common Public Attribution License (CPAL)
timeline.snippet: Responds that OSI cannot realistically reverse its approval of APL without risking its trademark, and that mistakes in past approvals are simply unavoidable.
timeline.point_zh: 回应称 OSI 无法在不危及商标的情况下撤销对 APL 的批准，过去的批准失误是不可避免的。
timeline.point: Responds that OSI cannot realistically reverse its approval of APL without risking its trademark, and that mistakes in past approvals are simply unavoidable.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Common Public Attribution License (CPAL)
timeline.snippet: Counters that requiring arbitrary graphics on GUIs (e.g. phones that can only display one image) violates OSD #10, that OSD was derived from DFSG and not industry realities, and that the Larger Work provision plus attribution requirements ultimately makes combining programs impractical, amounting to an OSD #3 concern.
timeline.point_zh: 反驳称要求 GUI 显示任意图形（如只能显示一张图的手机）违反 OSD #10，OSD 源自 DFSG 而非行业现实，且“更大作品”条款加上署名要求最终会使程序合并不切实际，构成 OSD #3 问题。
timeline.point: Counters that requiring arbitrary graphics on GUIs (e.g. phones that can only display one image) violates OSD #10, that OSD was derived from DFSG and not industry realities, and that the Larger Work provision plus attribution requirements ultimately makes combining programs impractical, amounting to an OSD #3 concern.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Common Public Attribution License (CPAL)
timeline.snippet: Agrees logo-accumulation is a theoretical concern but urges proportionality, arguing the logo-overload scenario is a severe over-exaggeration unlikely to occur in practice, and that reviewers should tolerate such unlikely licence-created problem scenarios.
timeline.point_zh: 同意 logo 堆积在理论上是问题，但主张应保持比例感，认为 logo 过载情景是对现实严重夸大且极不可能发生，建议评审者容忍此类不太可能发生的许可证问题情景。
timeline.point: Agrees logo-accumulation is a theoretical concern but urges proportionality, arguing the logo-overload scenario is a severe over-exaggeration unlikely to occur in practice, and that reviewers should tolerate such unlikely licence-created problem scenarios.

status_review.rationale: Human-calibrated baseline restore after concurrent-run corruption.

submissions.name: Educational Community License, Version 2.0
aliases: For Approval: ECL 2.0

board_vote.motion_text: GPLv3 & LGPLv3 — we approve these licenses with the following statement: “The Open Source Initiative is pleased to announce that, based on broad review and acceptance by both the Board and the community, it has confirmed that GPLv3 and LGPLv3 both conform to the Open Source Definition. Note that new licenses containing “further restrictions” allowed by GPLv3 and LGPLv3 may not be conformant with the OSD, and thus will still require separate review and approval. Due to the dramatic differences between and viable communities around both the GPLv3 family and the GPLv2 family of licenses, we will not be marking GPLv2 and LGPLv2 as redundant, even thought they are technically superseded respectively by GPLv3 and LGPLv3.”

timeline.subject: For Approval: ECL 2.0
timeline.snippet: Summarizes the ECL 2.0 discussion and respectfully requests approval, noting net-zero proliferation impact, the explicit patent-grant rationale, and that one of two raised issues has been addressed.
timeline.point_zh: 总结 ECL 2.0 讨论，正式请求批准；强调对许可证增殖净影响为零、明确专利授权的理由，并说明所提两项问题中已解决一项。
timeline.point: Summarizes the ECL 2.0 discussion and respectfully requests approval, noting net-zero proliferation impact, the explicit patent-grant rationale, and that one of two raised issues has been addressed.

timeline.subject: For Approval: ECL 2.0
timeline.snippet: Finds the net-zero rationale compelling enough not to oppose approval, but still prefers Apache 2.0; outlines concerns about recipient burden and patent-retention, then calls for a vote.
timeline.point_zh: 认为「净零增殖」理由颇具说服力、不再反对批准，但仍倾向 Apache 2.0；列举对用户负担与专利保留的担忧，随后呼吁付诸表决。
timeline.point: Finds the net-zero rationale compelling enough not to oppose approval, but still prefers Apache 2.0; outlines concerns about recipient burden and patent-retention, then calls for a vote.

board_vote.motion_text: GPLv3 & LGPLv3 — we approve these licenses with the following statement: “The Open Source Initiative is pleased to announce that, based on broad review and acceptance by both the Board and the community, it has confirmed that GPLv3 and LGPLv3 both conform to the Open Source Definition. Note that new licenses containing “further restrictions” allowed by GPLv3 and LGPLv3 may not be conformant with the OSD, and thus will still require separate review and approval. Due to the dramatic differences between and viable communities around both the GPLv3 family and the GPLv2 family of licenses, we will not be marking GPLv2 and LGPLv2 as redundant, even thought they are technically superseded respectively by GPLv3 and LGPLv3.”

license_texts.text:
Simple Public License 
                                Version 0.9

Definitions to make the rest of the text flow more naturally. 

Any member of the public can be "You" in this license, although
each member of the public makes their own separate agreement with
the copyright owner.

"We" is a bit more tricky. At first glance it just looks like it's 
talking about me, the original author. But gradually it will grow to
include anyone who has ever contributed code to the software--they 
are a copyright holder, and will be part of the definition of "we" 
for people who receive code from them.

Since "our software" isn't well defined I expect people to put notices
on their software itself declaring that it is subject to this agreement.
We are willing to license our software to you at no charge only on the
condition that you accept all of the terms of this agreement: please
note the broad disclaimers of warranty and liability. You indicate
your acceptance of these terms by using our software.

I want to make it clear that the software cannot be used unless you 
agree to the terms of this license, and also try and make the disclaimers
at the end a bit more conspicuous by drawing attention to them in
the first section.

I am a bit worried about the acceptance criteria but this seems to be 
what most free software licenses do.
(1) "YOU MAY USE OUR SOFTWARE FOR FREE"

You may use and copy our software, or a compiled version of it, and you
may distribute, display, perform, and include as part of an aggregate
collection, verbatim copies of our software.

You should be able to download the software and use it on your computers, 
and you should be able to give verbatim copies of it, exactly as you 
received them, to anyone you want to. 

This might not let you created compiled binaries and distribute them, 
but you should be able to do that under section 3 if not.
(2) "YOU MAY CREATE NON-FREE APPLICATIONS"
You may create a derivative work based on our software by combining a 
complete unmodified copy of our software, or a compiled version it, with 
your own separate source materials. You may license the work directly to 
third party end users. Subject to your license, recipients may use the 
work on one or more computers, and may create backup copies of it, but may 
not otherwise copy, distribute, lend, sublicense, or adapt it.

If someone is just using the software to provide solutions to end users, 
and what they are doing isn't so much an improvement on my software as 
a plain old use of it, then I don't want them to be copylefted. This 
is basically a hole in the copyleft in section 3. 

The restrictions here are:

  o Your use of it doesn't require you to alter the original software,
    you work from an "unmodified" copy--presumably basically what you
    downloaded, only you probably compiled it first. 

  o You aren'te altering the software itself, but rather using it as 
    a part of a larger product--you have your own separate materials
    to add in to the mixture

  o You are providing the software directly to your customers, and 
    they are just simple end-users. In other words, you are not 
    mass marketing a development tool, or something else that might
    be a competing version of the free software (and thus an
    improvement that is not being shared).

  o The end users get only very limited rights: just enough rights to
    be end users. The derived work is a dead end--it can't propagate
    any further than this.

  o You are allowed to charge these end users money for creating 
    this stuff for them, and add your own license restrictions on
    top of the ones already imposed by this agreement. 
(3) "YOU MUST SHARE IMPROVEMENTS TO OUR SOFTWARE"
You may create other derivative works based on our software but you must
immediately make them available to the public, including all source code, 
free of charge, on or through a medium customarily used for software 
exchange. Recipients automatically receive an irrevocable joint offer from 
you and from us to use your work under the terms of this agreement, 
royalty-free, and without restriction. You grant to us an irrevocable, 
non-exclusive, worldwide license to all intellectual property associated 
with alterations to the literal source code, structure, sequence, or 
organization of our software itself.

This is intended to be a generic copyleft and should apply to any 
derived work that doesn't fit the definition in section 2. I think
this clause provides me some of my "consideration", in the form of 
source code I expect to receive, under contract law.

I am a bit worried that the word "other" might not be appropriate,
but I can't see what other interpretation of it there can be--there
is only one other way to create derived works mentioned in the
license.

I say you must "immediately" make the work available to the public. That
might be too strong--the reason for this phrase is to catch people who 
write application servers. They make an improvement to my software, and
then make it available to people through an application server that 
runs on a publically networked machine. Since people link to the app 
server, the software is never distributed, and a GPL style distribution
copyleft would not force these improvements to be shared. It would be
nice if I could come up with an effective clause here that was not 
so heavy handed, but I couldn't think of it. I tried using the idea
of "public performance" at one point, but nobody could agree on what
that meant for software.

The "on or through a medium customarily used for software exchange" is
intended to allow people to either email the stuff to me, or to post it
on their website and tell me to look there. In the latter case, I would 
not expect them to have to notify me every time they changed something.
It should be good enough that they told me to check the website from 
time to time to see what their current version is. Alternately, they 
could open up access to their CVS archive, or something different. 

I use the phrase "joint offer from you and from us" because I don't 
think any rights attach to the software itself. I think recipients 
have to get their copyright license from all the copyright holders.
This phrase will recursively grow to include everyone who has ever
contributed code, since a contributor becomes part of "us" when
a third party gets the code.

This paragraph also gives "us" unrestricted rights to the modifications
that other people make to the software. Out of all the people that are
included in "us", only the original developer will have accumulated 
these license grants for all of the contributions. This allows me
to grant people exemptions if it turns out that their use of the 
software would be forbidden but I think it should be allowed. It would
also allow me to relicense the software under other terms. 

However, I don't want this grant of rights to wind up including 
anything that is not really a part of my program. I think the 
phrase "literal source code, structure, sequence, or organization"
catches any improvement to the program that really affects the 
program itself in some way--and doesn't just link the program in.
Your your derivative work must be unencumbered: it must not depend on 
additional software unless that software is distributed to the public under 
a license which allows everyone to use, copy, and distribute the software 
royalty-free; also, under any patent claim licensable by you which would be 
infringed by the use of the work under this agreement, you grant to each 
recipient a worldwide non-exclusive, royalty-free patent license to use, 
sell, import, and transfer the work under the terms of this agreement.


I have a mini-definition of "kind of free" software here. I specifically 
want people to be able to write software that depends on the Java JRE
(the Java virtual machine), which you are allowed to copy, distribute,
and use. But you aren't allowed to make modifications to the JRE.

However, I don't want people writing "improvements" to my software that
wind up making it depend on something they sell, or being subject to 
some patent they can later claim against people. 
(4) "YOU MUST CREDIT US"
If you distribute, display, or perform our software or a derivative work 
based on it then you must attach our copyright notices and give prominent 
notice that you used our software under this agreement. You must ensure
that these notices appear wherever authors of the work are credited. You 
must also include a copy of this agreement when you distribute any work 
subject to it.

Here is some more of my "consideration" under contract law. I want some
free advertising in exchange for writing free software. If you use my 
software, then in your "About" and "Credits" box, I want you to mention
my copyrights. I'm hoping this is a weak enough credit clause that it 
doesn't burden people the way that the BSD advertising clause does. I
just don't want the credit of me buried in some user manual that 
nobody would ever read, or only appear in the source code, which no 
end user would ever see.
(5) "GENERAL TERMS AND CONDITIONS"
This agreement represents the entire agreement between us, and it is 
effective until our copyright expires. Your rights under this agreement 
will terminate immediately, without notice from us, if you fail to comply 
with any of its provisions, infringe on our copyright, or file any 
litigation against us relating to our software. Upon such termination you 
must immediately cease all use, copying, and distribution of our software 
and derivatives of it. However, you may continue to distribute complete, 
unmodified copies of our software as part of any existing aggregate 
collection for up to one further year.

I think I have to specify a term for the agreement, so I picked the 
lifetime of the copyright. 

I wanted to spell out that you have to stop using the software in 
case you violate the license in some way. Also, I wanted to ward off 
some lawsuits by terminating peoples rights in the event that they 
bring a lawsuit back against me. I hope this doesn't get me into 
trouble with "restraint of trade" laws or some legal principle. 

The clause about aggregate works is there to save CD manufacturers 
from having to recall a million CD's. If someone violates the license,
maybe by accident, but before anyone noticed the violation got printed
on a million CD's, it would be unfair to force an expensive recall of
all of those CD's. I would rather they just stuck in a note or published
a statement notifying everyone that the copy of my software on the CD 
was unlawfull and couldn't be used. I'm not particular on exactly what
they do as long as it's reasonable and they stop infringing.
For the sole purpose of taking action against an infringer of our
copyrights, including actions seeking remedies, compensation, or the
recovery of damages, anyone engaged in the lawful distribution of our 
software shall be considered a beneficial owner of the rights to copy and 
distribute it, and therefore has the authority to pursue such actions.

This is one of my big ideas, and no doubt the most controversial bit 
in this license. I stole the phrase "beneficial owner" from the US 
copyright act, where it is used to describe the rights of television
broadcasters who have licensed the right to broadcast a TV show, and 
then some pirate in their jurisdiction broadcasts it as well--costing
them advertising revenue. The copyright act says they are "beneficial
owners" and can therefore take the pirate to court, even if they can't
get the co-operation of the original author.

I think that a copyleft is *for* the community just as much as it is 
*for* the developer. A lot of people choose to use copylefted software
precisely because they know that they can take the project over if 
the original developer leaves. 

As a result, they are willing to contribute ideas, code, suggestions, 
help test the software, and basically put some effort into the code. 
They may even have chosen copylefted software, as opposed to some other
opensource software, because they know that ensures they will have
access to all of the improvements. 

If the original developer leaves they lose all of those benefits, and
I think that is not fair. I am trying to find some way to express that
the community has an interest in the software, and therefore should have
the right to go to court and defend that interest.

My concern here is that I may have given anyone who distributes the
software authority to rewrite the license. That needs to be restricted
in some way--I want them to be able to put a stop to license violations,
but not settle the case by granting the infringer extra rights. I don't
really know what to do here, but I really do want people to be able 
to back up the software they use.

Also it occurs to me that some tiny little free software developer may
not look like much of a threat to a large corporation with a huge legal
team. The large company might feel they can win any infringement case 
just on the basis of having a better legal team. This clause should 
strike some fear into them, because any free software distributor (and
some are very large) could bring their legal team to court as well.
Nothing in this agreement shall be interpreted strictly against us. If
any provision of this agreement is ruled invalid, the rest shall remain
in effect, and the invalid provision shall be reformed to the minimum
extent necessary to make it valid. If a new version of this agreement
is published by Semiotek Inc. you may opt to use your copy of our
software under the terms of the new version so published.

I know the "strictly against us" stuff isn't likely to fly in all 
regions, but again I figure free software developers are likely to

the community has an interest in the software, and therefore should have

just on the basis of having a better legal team. This clause should
strike some fear into them, because any free software distributor (and

timeline.subject: For Approval: Simple Public License (SimPL)
timeline.snippet: Submits the Simple Public License for discussion as a simpler GPL 2.0-like license intended to preserve GPL coverage and compatibility.
timeline.point_zh: 提交 Simple Public License 供讨论，称其是更简单的 GPL 2.0 类许可证，旨在保留 GPL 的覆盖范围和兼容性。
timeline.point: Submits the Simple Public License for discussion as a simpler GPL 2.0-like license intended to preserve GPL coverage and compatibility.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Simple Public License (SimPL)
timeline.snippet: Opposes SimPL as another likely minority license, arguing that new licenses fragment and slow free and open source software adoption.
timeline.point_zh: 反对 SimPL，认为它可能只是另一个少数派许可证，新许可证会分裂并拖慢自由和开源软件采用。
timeline.point: Opposes SimPL as another likely minority license, arguing that new licenses fragment and slow free and open source software adoption.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Simple Public License (SimPL)
timeline.snippet: Argues SimPL could allow relicensing, but its patent-termination clause should be narrowed to affected distributors and actual compliance conflicts.
timeline.point_zh: 主张 SimPL 可以允许再许可，但其专利终止条款应限于受影响分发者和实际合规冲突。
timeline.point: Argues SimPL could allow relicensing, but its patent-termination clause should be narrowed to affected distributors and actual compliance conflicts.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Simple Public License (SimPL)
timeline.snippet: Critiques SimPL as missing many GPL protections and clarifications, while acknowledging some proposed compatibility and notice improvements.
timeline.point_zh: 批评 SimPL 缺少许多 GPL 的保护和澄清，同时认可若干兼容性和通知方面的改进。
timeline.point: Critiques SimPL as missing many GPL protections and clarifications, while acknowledging some proposed compatibility and notice improvements.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Simple Public License (SimPL)
timeline.snippet: Continues critiquing SimPL details, recommending clearer GPL-like terms on notices, third-party licensing, royalty-free grants, source form, and patents.
timeline.point_zh: 继续批评 SimPL 细节，建议在通知、第三方许可、免版税授权、源码形式和专利方面采用更清晰的 GPL 式条款。
timeline.point: Continues critiquing SimPL details, recommending clearer GPL-like terms on notices, third-party licensing, royalty-free grants, source form, and patents.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Simple Public License (SimPL)
timeline.snippet: Reviews revised SimPL language favorably in places but identifies remaining issues around license announcement, compatibility chains, source offers, and export clauses.

timeline.point: Reports final SimPL revisions, accepts the suggested compatibility wording, and asks the board to consider SimPL in June.

timeline.snippet: Submits Artistic License 2.0 for approval, describing improvements over 1.0 in readability and legal precision, new relicensing and patent clauses, and upstream/downstream compatibility details.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Artistic License 2.0
timeline.snippet: Acknowledges the license is clearly free and open source but questions whether clause 6 allows proprietary modifications, as it does not seem to require source distribution for modified versions.
timeline.point_zh: 认为该许可证明显是自由开源的，但质疑第6条是否允许专有修改版本（未要求分发修改版源码）。
timeline.point: Acknowledges the license is clearly free and open source but questions whether clause 6 allows proprietary modifications, as it does not seem to require source distribution for modified versions.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Artistic License 2.0
timeline.snippet: Concedes that the Artistic License is not copyleft, but finds clause 6 wording unclear and suggests a clearer alternative phrasing.
timeline.point_zh: 承认 Artistic License 非著佐权，但认为第6条措辞不清，建议改为更明确的表达。
timeline.point: Concedes that the Artistic License is not copyleft, but finds clause 6 wording unclear and suggests a clearer alternative phrasing.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Artistic License 2.0
timeline.snippet: Responds to feedback, explaining that definitions are ordered by logical concept progression to improve readability, and that introducing an indirect "License Steward" layer would reduce clarity.

timeline.point: Responds to feedback, explaining that definitions are ordered by logical concept progression to improve readability, and that introducing an indirect "License Steward" layer would reduce clarity.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Artistic License 2.0
timeline.snippet: Questions whether binary distributions can bypass section 4, specifically whether one could create a proprietary version named "perl" without distributing source code.
