timeline.point: Argues that allowing private modifications places restrictions on source code, contradicting the spirit of "libre."

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Thu, Aug 8, 2019 at 9:44 PM Moritz Maxeiner <mm at ucw.sh> wrote: > In my opinion the spirit (if not the wording) of the "libre" in FLOSS is > primarily (and if not should be)
timeline.point: Argues that disallowing privacy restricts source code creation and does not protect liberty.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Friday, 9 August 2019 05:36:26 CEST Russell McOrmond wrote: > On Thu, Aug 8, 2019 at 9:44 PM Moritz Maxeiner <mm at ucw.sh> wrote: > > In my opinion the spirit (if not the word
timeline.point: Disagrees with equating derived source code with personal information and prioritizes releasing derivative works.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Fri, Aug 9, 2019 at 8:45 AM Moritz Maxeiner <mm at ucw.sh> wrote: > On Friday, 9 August 2019 05:36:26 CEST Russell McOrmond wrote: > > Curious: Since I have the capability to w
timeline.point: Asserts that authors should not control private software activities and labels such control as proprietary.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Tue, Aug 13, 2019 at 7:34 PM Russell McOrmond <russellmcormond at gmail.com> wrote: > Is it the act of me typing the software into my computer that offends you? > Obviously, th
timeline.point: States that creating derivative works is restricted by copyright even in private, and authors choose to permit it.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 14, 2019 at 1:30 AM Bruce Perens via License-discuss < license-discuss at lists.opensource.org> wrote: > On Tue, Aug 13, 2019 at 7:34 PM Russell McOrmond < > russellmc
timeline.point: Asks whether OSD-compliant licenses should embrace harmful legal restrictions on private activities simply because they exist.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 14, 2019 at 7:15 AM Russell McOrmond <russellmcormond at gmail.com> wrote: > a) whether these restrictions of private activities should be considered > consistent with
timeline.point: States that OSD rules do not protect private activities from the terms of Open Source licenses.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 14, 2019 at 12:47 PM Bruce Perens via License-discuss < license-discuss at lists.opensource.org> wrote: The OSD rules don't protect your private activities from the te
timeline.point: Argues that OSD #3 implies a license forbidding private modifications is not an open source license.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 14, 2019 at 1:45 PM John Cowan <cowan at ccil.org> wrote: > I think that OSD #3 does exactly that. "The license must allow > modifications and derived works [...]" A l
timeline.point: Clarifies that the discussion concerns when distribution terms activate for derivative works, not forbidding the act itself.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Thanks for the clarification. I simply reacted to your saying that private modifications are not necessarily protected by OSD-compliant licenses. On Wed, Aug 14, 2019 at 4:53 PM B
timeline.point: Thanks the sender for the clarification on private modifications and OSD compliance.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wednesday, 14 August 2019 04:33:25 CEST Russell McOrmond wrote: > On Fri, Aug 9, 2019 at 8:45 AM Moritz Maxeiner <mm at ucw.sh> wrote: > > On Friday, 9 August 2019 05:36:26 CES
timeline.point: Objects to secret derivative works and argues the OSD does not conflict with requiring distribution upon creation.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 12:38 PM Moritz Maxeiner <mm at ucw.sh> wrote: > Why does my wish for derivative works of certain software to be available > to > the public (and legitimat
timeline.point: Reiterates opposition to regulating private activities and argues private acts do not constitute "derivative works."

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 11:00 AM Russell McOrmond <russellmcormond at gmail.com> wrote: > > I am offended by any alleged legitimacy granted to the exclusive rights of > software a
timeline.point: Advises maintaining a collegial tone and questions the limits of protecting private acts that infringe copyright.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Russell McOrmond wrote: > > On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 12:38 PM Moritz Maxeiner <mm at ucw.sh> wrote: > > Why does my wish for derivative works of certain software to be available to
timeline.point: Expresses offense at users benefiting from free code while keeping improvements private.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 11:16 AM Howard Chu <hyc at openldap.org> wrote: > I am offended by the notion that someone may benefit from code that I > released for free, but > would d
timeline.point: Questions how sharing something under specific terms grants others the fundamental right to do as they wish in private.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 2:23 PM Bruce Perens <bruce at perens.com> wrote: > > > On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 11:16 AM Howard Chu <hyc at openldap.org> wrote: > >> I am offended by the
timeline.point: Argues that copyright is a public bargain with limits, and private activities should be carved out of regulation.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: > You are trying to state copyright law in reverse, presuming the right to control culture and science is natural and any limitations on that (such as the protection of privacy ri
timeline.point: Notes the moral conflict between personal liberty and creator control, believing private-use restrictions are not in society's best interest.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Russell McOrmond wrote: > > > On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 2:23 PM Bruce Perens <bruce at perens.com <mailto:bruce at perens.com>> wrote: > > > > On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 11:16 AM Howar
timeline.point: Argues that authors own their work and users have zero rights without abiding by license terms, asserting an obligation to contribute back to prevent maintainer burnout.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Hi all, On Wed, Aug 21, 2019, at 12:22, Howard Chu wrote: > Article 27: > (1) Everyone has the right freely to participate in the cultural life > of the community, to enjoy the ar
timeline.point: Warns that forced disclosure of private modifications could endanger users in humanitarian contexts and is contrary to the OSD.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 21, 2019, 15:22 Howard Chu <hyc at openldap.org> wrote: > Russell McOrmond wrote: > When you benefit from Free software, you have an obligation to contribute > back, e
timeline.point: States that obligations to provide cash or labor are fundamentally incompatible with open source licenses and would have killed GPLv3 adoption.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 2:38 PM Bruce Perens via License-discuss < license-discuss at lists.opensource.org> wrote: > > > On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 11:00 AM Russell McOrmond < > russ
timeline.point: Argues that regulating private activities via copyright is a policy overreach and that Free and Open Source licenses should exclude such restrictions to protect user freedoms.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 3:39 PM Christopher Sean Morrison via License-discuss <license-discuss at lists.opensource.org> wrote: > > You are trying to state copyright law in reverse
timeline.point: Explains that software licensing is a policy matter influencing legal precedent and clarifies that owning copyright is not like owning physical copies.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 2:16 PM Howard Chu <hyc at openldap.org> wrote: > Fwiw, most of the free software I released in the 1980s, before GPL > existed, had the clause > "You are
timeline.point: Contends that forcing private modifications to become contributions contradicts the FSF's Freedom 0 and the OSD, focusing on public interest over proprietary interests.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Russell McOrmond wrote: > > On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 2:16 PM Howard Chu <hyc at openldap.org <mailto:hyc at openldap.org>> wrote: > > Fwiw, most of the free software I released in
timeline.point: Asserts that requesting improvements benefits the greater good and prevents zero-day vulnerabilities, arguing the FSF erred by not enforcing contribution obligations.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wednesday, 21 August 2019 22:07:28 CEST Michael Downey wrote: > Hi all, > > On Wed, Aug 21, 2019, at 12:22, Howard Chu wrote: > > Article 27: > > (1) Everyone has the right fre
timeline.point: Suggests restricting private modifications is acceptable for software like compilers, while distinguishing between software use and private derivative work creation.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Russell, please clarify something for me about your opinion about copyright policy: Is any license whatsoever required in order for a private party to copy or modify a work of sof
timeline.point: Asks for clarification on whether a license is required for private copying or modification under copyright law, assuming software is copyrightable.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wednesday, 21 August 2019 19:59:03 CEST Russell McOrmond wrote: > On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 12:38 PM Moritz Maxeiner <mm at ucw.sh> wrote: > > Why does my wish for derivative wor
timeline.point: Defends the legitimacy of copyright holder concerns and criticizes the previous implication as hostile, bowing out of the sub-thread.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Howard Chu dixit: >A standard license clause of this form would also have ended the >debate over disclosure of zero-day vulnerabilities and other such >nonsense that plagues today
timeline.point: Cites the Debian Free Software Guidelines to argue that licenses coercing recipients regarding private modifications are unacceptable and endanger users.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: > > You are trying to state copyright law in reverse, presuming the right to control culture and science is natural and any limitations on that (such as the protection of privacy
timeline.point: Rejects the notion that advocating for creator rights is illegitimate, arguing it is consistent with the OSD and a complex issue.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 8:39 PM Lawrence Rosen <lrosen at rosenlaw.com> wrote: > Russell, please clarify something for me about your opinion about > copyright policy: Is any licen
timeline.point: Offers a policy opinion that the FSF and OSI should reject licenses regulating private modification, noting copyright law varies by jurisdiction.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Russell, what you said is not true in the United States. I dare not speak to Canadian law. Russell wrote: * What is the purpose of the copying or modification of the work. If the
timeline.point: Corrects the previous statement regarding US copyright law, asserting that compatibility modifications and backups generally require a license.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Thorsten Glaser wrote: > Howard Chu dixit: > >> A standard license clause of this form would also have ended the >> debate over disclosure of zero-day vulnerabilities and other su
timeline.point: Disagrees with the desert island test, arguing that sending modifications back doesn't immediately publish them and best-effort reporting is reasonable.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Thursday 22 August 2019 06:17, Howard Chu wrote: > The requirement to send modifications back doesn't prevent anyone from using the code. You > could call it best-effort, or at
timeline.point: Clarifies that in Free Software, the requirement to send modifications back applies only upon distribution, not for in-house changes.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Thu, Aug 22, 2019, 00:18 Howard Chu <hyc at openldap.org> wrote: > I don't believe this test is conclusive. Sending modifications back to the > code's original author doesn't i
timeline.point: Argues that privileging the original author creates badgeware, requiring publication of private changesets is ineffective, and the license seeks proprietary control.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Johnny A. Solbu dixit: >On Thursday 22 August 2019 06:17, Howard Chu wrote: >> Two of these which often appear necessary are the Chinese Dissident >> test (requirement to publish
timeline.point: Insists that the desert island test is valid and that Free Software never requires sending modifications back, only passing them along to recipients.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Thursday 22 August 2019 20:55, Thorsten Glaser wrote: > Some Free Software has a requirement to pass the modifications along to the > recipient if you distribute the work, but
timeline.point: Clarifies that the previous comment was referencing Linus Torvalds' view that publishing changes on a project site counts as sending code back.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Johnny A. Solbu dixit: >He have said in inverviews that he wants code back. He wants the >changes people use, but says that publishing the changed code on the >projects own site i
timeline.point: Notes that while projects often want code back, the actual license only requires distributing source to recipients, not sending it to upstream.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On 8/21/2019 7:33 PM, Lawrence Rosen wrote: > > Russell, please clarify something for me about your opinion about > copyright policy: Is any license whatsoever required in order f
timeline.point: Expresses confusion about fair use in software and questions whether OSI should support licenses that weaken it.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 11:35 PM Lawrence Rosen <lrosen at rosenlaw.com> wrote: > I appreciate your discussion of preferred policies, but that has nothing > to do with license-dis
timeline.point: Argues that clarifying the line between proprietor and user interests is the purpose of the OSD and that license interpretation by courts is on-topic.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Roger Fujii wrote: > Now I'm confused. Are you saying there is no "fair use" when the target is software? While one can weaken" fair use" via the license, is this a good idea for
timeline.point: Clarifies that fair use is a defense to infringement but a poor basis for claiming rights to commercial software distribution.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Russell McOrmond wrote: > Guesses about license interpretation by courts, and unintended consequences from that interpretation of licenses, is entirely on-topic for this forum. Th
timeline.point: Acknowledges that policy guesses cannot override court interpretations of existing law, citing the API copyright exception as an example.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On 8/23/2019 1:23 PM, Lawrence Rosen wrote: > > Roger Fujii wrote: > > Now I'm confused. Are you saying there is no "fair use" when the > target is software? While one can weaken"
timeline.point: Argues that if fair use is a right, some modifications should be covered, and suggests licenses and OSI should clarify their stance on fair use.
